Event

Track

Solicitation

Submitter
Mycosoft, LLC · CAGE 9KR60 · UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9
PI / POC
Morgan Rockcoons, Founder & CEO · morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077
Handling
UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARY
Version
FormSpace overlay v1.0 — 2026-09-01
1. Overview — Pattern as Class Discovery in Form Space
Pattern Analysis is the operation of identifying Form-equivalence classes over an ordered stream of
multi-modal observations. Given the learned signal map Λ: X → Z and the quotient F_Λ = X/~Λ, a
pattern is a temporally coherent cluster of observations that map to a common region of F_Λ. The
Nature Learning Model estimates the posterior over latent state q_θ(s_t | o_{1:t}); the pattern score
is the log-likelihood that consecutive windows share an equivalence class under the learned
tolerance.
2. Method — Selective State-Space Backbone
We use a selective state-space (SSM/Mamba-style) backbone with input-dependent Δt, B, C
parameters. The backbone runs at three tier sizes: 120 M (edge), 500 M (ITDX-preferred), and 1.5 B
(stretch). Training objectives include masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment across
modalities, physics regularization, calibration (Brier + Expected Calibration Error), graph
consistency, causal invariance, and a composite safety loss (10 loss terms total; see Evaluation
Harness).
Two baselines run before the learned model in every evaluation:
•  Deterministic: robust z-score with median/MAD normalization plus persistence window (see
Coastal Sentinel §8.1 for the equation).
•  Modern sequence baseline: matched-data-split transformer at equivalent parameter count.
3. Inputs
•  Rooted observations per canonical schema (identity, time, uncertainty, location, uncertainty,
modality, calibrated features, quality, raw ref, hash).
•  Device-health and link-state streams from the DIRTNet 4-node emulator.
•  Controlled-stimulus truth markers with disclosed labels.
•  Optional human adjudication where available.
4. Outputs
•  Anomaly score per observation and per window.
•  Ranked Form-class candidates with confidence.
•  Time-to-detection against truth markers.

MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 Task 12 — Pattern Analysis — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 2
•  Calibrated confidence with uncertainty decomposition (aleatoric + epistemic).
•  Evidence IDs and Merkle-verified lineage.
•  Explicit missing-modality flags and calibration age.
5. Field Ablations (run on every evaluation)
•  Remove FCI (bioelectric) channel.
•  Remove Agaric imagery.
•  Remove Psathyrella acoustic context.
•  Inject 250 ms clock error.
•  Inject 5% packet delay.
•  Inject linear sensor drift.
•  Compare centralized-raw versus edge-features-plus-signed-provenance.
6. Metrics
•  Precision / recall / F1 with grouped bootstrap over 5 seeds {11,17,23,29,31}.
•  Time-to-detection distribution (median + 95% CI).
•  Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score.
•  Class-stability across seeds — do the same equivalence classes recover under seed
variation?
•  Node-dropout degradation curve.
•  Conformal prediction interval width at α = 0.1.
7. Timing Budget (live, on-site)
•  Cold start ≤ 30 s.
•  Live inference ≤ 90 s total on the on-site sample.
•  Memory gate: 80% VRAM ceiling triggers automatic tier downgrade with visible UI label.
8. Failure Modes and Fallback Ladder
The fallback ladder is: medium → small → quantized → distilled → classical → prerecorded → static.
Every fallback state is labeled in the operator UI so an Army SME can tell exactly which mode is
running. A single drifting sensor is expected to shift the Form-class boundary; NLM must
downgrade confidence and flag calibration rather than silently accept the drifted stream.
9. Underperformance Statement
If the live configuration does not meet its preregistered target, the PI states on the record: the
observed metric, the preregistered target, the deterministic-baseline value, and that the run is
signed and reproducible. We do not attempt to fix failing runs live.
Morgan Rockcoons
Founder & CEO, Mycosoft, LLC
morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077

pages.text:
MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 Architecture One-Pager — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 1
Architecture One-Pager — ITDX26
Observation-to-action pipeline; role boundaries
Layered architecture
Physical world: air · soil · mycelium · water · sound · light · movement · weather
Droid body layer: deterministic acquisition, calibration, local limits, health
Edge cortex: Jetson / NPU / TinyML — fingerprints, anomaly scores, NLM state, compression
Evidence contract: rooted observation — identity, time, location, calibration, quality, raw ref, hash
Mycorrhizae + DIRTNet: pub/sub, link selection, routing, store-forward, partition recovery
MINDEX: time series, graph, vector, raw refs, command records, Merkle epochs
NLM / FUSARIUM: state + pattern estimation, typed graph analysis
MYCA scenario runtime: role assignment, hypothesis generation, COA proposal
AVANI gate: deterministic admissibility — PASS / REVIEW / DENY / PAUSE
Bounded command intent → local droid safety controller → ACK + outcome evidence
Earth Simulator / CREP / replay: operator projection with uncertainty and labels
Role boundaries
•  NLM estimates state and uncertainty. It does not act.
•  FUSARIUM analyzes graphs and relationships. It does not act.
•  MYCA orchestrates algorithms and proposes COAs. It does not directly actuate.
•  AVANI constrains action; requires human approval for high-risk actions.
•  MINDEX preserves lineage. It does not decide.
•  CREP / Earth Simulator presents evidence. It does not conclude.
Product-compute rule
Compute runs on the droids and field gateway according to capability tier. The ITDX laptops are
interfaces and evaluation surfaces. They are not the reason the product works and must not be
described as the product architecture.
Morgan Rockcoons
Founder & CEO, Mycosoft, LLC
morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077

pages.text:
-- STAGED MIGRATION — DO NOT APPLY DIRECTLY TO PRODUCTION
-- MINDEX Form Space Advanced Research Layer
-- Run only after 00XX_form_space_core.sql and core API/outbox validation.

BEGIN;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.basin (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  attractor_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.attractor(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  boundary_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  membership_model_ref text,
  volume_estimate jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  confidence double precision CHECK (confidence IS NULL OR confidence BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  evidence_root text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','supported','falsified','retired')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_basin_attractor ON form_space.basin(attractor_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_basin_chart ON form_space.basin(chart_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.boundary (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  boundary_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (boundary_type IN
      ('viability','ethical','physical','ecological','identity',
       'security','classification','unknown')),
  definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  avani_policy_ref text,
  severity text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'gate'
    CHECK (severity IN ('inform','warn','gate','veto')),
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','active','retired')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_boundary_space_type
  ON form_space.boundary(space_id, boundary_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_boundary_chart
  ON form_space.boundary(chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_boundary_model
  ON form_space.boundary(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.invariant (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  name text NOT NULL,
  invariant_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (invariant_type IN
      ('topological','geometric','functional','causal','goal',
       'repair','information','physical','unknown')),
  definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  tolerance jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  validation_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN ('candidate','supported','falsified','retired')),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, name)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_invariant_space ON form_space.invariant(space_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_invariant_chart ON form_space.invariant(chart_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.equivalence_class (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  equivalence_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  invariant_ids uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  mapping_model_ref text,
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN
      ('candidate','supported','cross_substrate_supported','falsified','retired')),
  evidence_root text,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_equivalence_space
  ON form_space.equivalence_class(space_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.equivalence_member (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  equivalence_class_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.equivalence_class(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  embodiment_binding_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.embodiment_binding(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  mapping_definition jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  membership_score double precision
    CHECK (membership_score IS NULL OR membership_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (state_id IS NOT NULL OR embodiment_binding_id IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_fs_equivalence_member_state
  ON form_space.equivalence_member(equivalence_class_id, system_id, state_id)
  WHERE state_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_equivalence_member_class
  ON form_space.equivalence_member(equivalence_class_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_equivalence_member_state
  ON form_space.equivalence_member(state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_equivalence_member_embodiment
  ON form_space.equivalence_member(embodiment_binding_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.cross_substrate_test (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  equivalence_class_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.equivalence_class(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  source_system_id text NOT NULL,
  target_system_id text NOT NULL,
  source_embodiment_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.embodiment_binding(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  target_embodiment_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.embodiment_binding(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  mapping_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  transition_error double precision
    CHECK (transition_error IS NULL OR transition_error >= 0),
  goal_error double precision
    CHECK (goal_error IS NULL OR goal_error >= 0),
  heldout_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned'
    CHECK (status IN ('planned','active','completed','failed','invalidated')),
  epistemic_result text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (epistemic_result IN ('pending','supported','inconclusive','falsified')),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (source_system_id <> target_system_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_xsub_equivalence
  ON form_space.cross_substrate_test(equivalence_class_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_xsub_source_embodiment
  ON form_space.cross_substrate_test(source_embodiment_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_xsub_target_embodiment
  ON form_space.cross_substrate_test(target_embodiment_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.goal_field (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  field_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  local_goal_components jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  conflict_index double precision
    CHECK (conflict_index IS NULL OR conflict_index BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  coherence_score double precision
    CHECK (coherence_score IS NULL OR coherence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  valid_from timestamptz NOT NULL,
  valid_until timestamptz,
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > valid_from)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_field_system_time
  ON form_space.goal_field(system_id, valid_from DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_field_space ON form_space.goal_field(space_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_field_chart ON form_space.goal_field(chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_field_target ON form_space.goal_field(target_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_field_model ON form_space.goal_field(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.coherence_event (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  goal_field_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.goal_field(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  event_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (event_type IN
      ('coherence_gain','coherence_loss','fragmentation',
       'coalition_change','local_defection','repair','unknown')),
  severity text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'info'
    CHECK (severity IN ('info','warning','critical')),
  score_before double precision
    CHECK (score_before IS NULL OR score_before BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  score_after double precision
    CHECK (score_after IS NULL OR score_after BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  evidence_refs jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_coherence_system_time

    CHECK (independence_score IS NULL OR independence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  stability_score double precision
    CHECK (stability_score IS NULL OR stability_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  causal_support double precision
    CHECK (causal_support IS NULL OR causal_support BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  complexity_penalty double precision
    CHECK (complexity_penalty IS NULL OR complexity_penalty >= 0),
  replication_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN ('candidate','supported','falsified','retired')),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_poly_system
  ON form_space.polycomputation(system_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_poly_trajectory
  ON form_space.polycomputation(trajectory_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.side_quest (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  polycomputation_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.polycomputation(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  description text NOT NULL,
  side_quest_score double precision
    CHECK (side_quest_score IS NULL OR side_quest_score >= 0),
  persistence_score double precision
    CHECK (persistence_score IS NULL OR persistence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  independence_score double precision
    CHECK (independence_score IS NULL OR independence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  revealed_preference_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  risk_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  anthropomorphic_interpretation_forbidden boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('candidate','replicating','supported','suppressed','sandboxed',
       'promoted','falsified','retired')),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_sidequest_system_status
  ON form_space.side_quest(system_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_sidequest_poly
  ON form_space.side_quest(polycomputation_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.rewrite_trial (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  original_target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  candidate_target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  intervention_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.intervention(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  pre_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  post_washout_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  posterior_shift jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  persistence_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  recovery_comparison jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned'
    CHECK (status IN ('planned','active','completed','failed','invalidated')),
  epistemic_result text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (epistemic_result IN
      ('pending','rewrite_supported','transient_only','inconclusive','falsified')),
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_rewrite_original
  ON form_space.rewrite_trial(original_target_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_rewrite_candidate
  ON form_space.rewrite_trial(candidate_target_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_rewrite_intervention
  ON form_space.rewrite_trial(intervention_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_rewrite_pre
  ON form_space.rewrite_trial(pre_state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_rewrite_post
  ON form_space.rewrite_trial(post_washout_state_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.psilo_session (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  requested_by text NOT NULL,
  scope jsonb NOT NULL,
  baseline_graph_ref text NOT NULL,
  phase text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'idle'
    CHECK (phase IN
      ('idle','onset','peak','comedown','integration','complete','killed')),
  dose_vector jsonb NOT NULL,
  hard_safety_policy_ref text NOT NULL,
  actions_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  started_at timestamptz,
  ended_at timestamptz,
  integration_report jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('draft','approved','active','paused','complete','killed','failed','vetoed')),
  correlation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (actions_enabled = false),
  CHECK (ended_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= started_at)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_psilo_status
  ON form_space.psilo_session(status, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.psilo_edge (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  session_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.psilo_session(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_node_id text NOT NULL,
  target_node_id text NOT NULL,
  edge_type text NOT NULL,
  weight double precision NOT NULL CHECK (weight >= 0),
  ttl interval NOT NULL CHECK (ttl > interval '0 seconds'),
  reason text NOT NULL,
  trust_evaluation jsonb NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  expired_at timestamptz,
  promoted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  CHECK (source_node_id <> target_node_id),
  CHECK (expires_at > created_at)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_psilo_edge_session
  ON form_space.psilo_edge(session_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_psilo_edge_expiry
  ON form_space.psilo_edge(expires_at)
  WHERE expired_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.psilo_afterimage (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  session_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.psilo_session(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  afterimage_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (afterimage_type IN
      ('candidate_edge','representation_bridge','hypothesis',
       'policy_change','agent_variant','other')),
  content jsonb NOT NULL,
  novelty_score double precision
    CHECK (novelty_score IS NULL OR novelty_score >= 0),
  validation_score double precision
    CHECK (validation_score IS NULL OR validation_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  risk_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  promotion_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (promotion_status IN
      ('candidate','testing','rejected','approved','promoted','retired')),
  sober_validation_ref text,
  evidence_root text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_psilo_afterimage_session
  ON form_space.psilo_afterimage(session_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.fci_trial (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  protocol_version text NOT NULL,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  organism_ref text,
  taxon_id uuid REFERENCES core.taxon(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  culture_or_site_ref text NOT NULL,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  goal_contract_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.goal_contract(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  baseline_window tstzrange NOT NULL,
  perturbation_plan jsonb NOT NULL,
  control_plan jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  washout_plan jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  observables jsonb NOT NULL,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  human_approval_ref text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('planned','approved','active','washout','completed','failed',
       'aborted','vetoed','invalidated')),
  evidence_root text,
  correlation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

  ON form_space.fci_trial(system_id, created_at DESC);

  ON form_space.fci_trial(taxon_id);

  ON form_space.fci_trial(space_id);

PI / POC
Morgan Rockcoons, Founder & CEO · morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077
Handling
UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARY
Version
FormSpace overlay v1.0 — 2026-09-01
1. Overview — Map as Inspectable Rendering
The Map Product is a deterministic projection of the state estimate from Form Space onto
Army-consumable geospatial coordinates, with uncertainty made visible. This task deliberately
uses no machine learning in the critical path. That is a maturity signal: we know when not to use the
model. The map renders what Tasks 12 and 13 produced; it does not reinterpret it.
2. Method — Deterministic Projection
Inputs from Tasks 12 and 13 are projected through a fixed function to produce:
•  Device positions and health status.
•  Direct and relayed communications paths (from DIRTNet routing).
•  Hazard proxy with uncertainty envelope (95% CI shading).
•  Tracks and standoff distances.
•  Event timeline with adjudication labels.
•  Evidence inspection panel (click-through to MINDEX records).
•  Classification / handling banner (UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARY for ITDX).
3. Fallback Ladder — Labeled in UI
The map explicitly labels its current data source in the operator UI at all times. The ladder is:
•  medium — full model output.
•  small — reduced-tier NLM output.
•  quantized — INT8 quantized inference.
•  distilled — student model output.
•  classical — deterministic baseline only.
•  prerecorded — signed replay from the field run.
•  static — last-known-good snapshot with timestamp.
An Army SME can tell exactly which mode is active by reading the label. This removes the failure
mode where a degraded system looks identical to a healthy one.
4. Outputs

MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 Task 14 — Map Product — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 2
•  Rendered map (PNG + interactive HTML replay).
•  Uncertainty overlay layer.
•  Fallback-state label with timestamp.
•  Merkle-verified evidence link for every rendered element.
5. Metrics
•  Cold start ≤ 30 s (deterministic path is fastest).
•  Refresh cadence ≤ 5 s per update.
•  Uncertainty-envelope coverage vs empirical error on ground-truth stimulus.
•  SME usability rating on a 5-point rubric.
6. Why No ML in the Critical Path
Learned components produce the underlying state estimate (Task 12) and the evidence graph
(Task 13). The map itself is a rendering function. Keeping the rendering deterministic means an
Army analyst can inspect exactly how a value on the map was computed by following the projection
chain backward to MINDEX. That audit path is a governance property, not a performance limitation.

pages.text:
FORM Space Source
NLM learns Form Space.MYCA navigates Form Space.FCI opens a bidirectional port into biological Form Space.PSILO temporarily expands and deforms MYCA’s accessible Form Space.MINDEX stores the Form Space Atlas and its evidence.HPL describes Form Space experiments and interventions.Mycorrhizae and DIRTNet distribute Form State and Goal Fields.Earth Simulator renders Form Space across geography and time.AVANI defines the viable, ethical, and admissible boundary.
A blueprint is now correctly defined as a target manifold, attractor, setpoint, or generative constraint within Form Space. It is not the name of the entire system.
What has been restored
1. Form Space as the canonical Mycosoft term
The document now defines Form Space as:
Mycosoft’s engineered, measurable space of possible organized states that a physical, biological, computational, ecological, robotic, or hybrid system can occupy, pursue, maintain, repair, transform into, or instantiate.
It explains why Mycosoft should use Form Space, rather than relying exclusively on:
Platonic Space
Morphospace
State space
Latent space
Design space
Solution space
Possibility space
Fitness landscape
Blueprint Space
The term works because form means both organized structure and the process of formation. It therefore includes not only anatomical shapes, but also:
Physiology
Homeostasis
Behavior
Policies
Memory
Identity
Goal structure
Computation
Collective organization
Ecological relationships
Repair and regeneration
Mind-like organization
Emergent competencies
“Space” gives the concept a rigorous engineering interpretation: coordinates, metrics, manifolds, topology, trajectories, fields, gradients, attractors, basins, barriers, reachability, controllability, curvature, uncertainty, and search.
The stronger Platonic interpretation remains explicitly identified as a research hypothesis, while Form Space is the measurable engineering layer. This follows Levin’s distinction between experimentally tractable morphogenetic navigation and his broader conjecture that physical embodiments may provide access to reusable patterns of form, behavior, and computation. (The Blog of Author Tim Ferriss)
2. The complete Form Space engineering vocabulary
The reconstruction now includes formal definitions for:
Form
Form Coordinate
Form Signature
Form Fingerprint
Form Manifold
Form Atlas
Form Chart
Form Graph
Form Hypergraph
Form Topology
Form Metric
Form Trajectory
Form Vector
Form Field
Form Gradient
Form Curvature
Blueprint
Target Manifold
Form Attractor
Form Basin
Form Barrier
Form Setpoint
Form Error
Form Memory
Form Repair
Form Regeneration
Form Plasticity
Form Drift
Identity Basin
Embodiment
Form Pointer
Form Accessibility
Form Affinity
Form Resonance
Form Bridge
Cross-Substrate Form Equivalence
Form Compiler
Form Transducer
Form Probe
Form Observer
Form Observatory
Form Side Quest
Form Wormhole
Form Safety Envelope
Form Lineage
Form Consolidation
Form Falsifier
These are not presented as terms already found verbatim in the source material. They are the proposed canonical Mycosoft engineering vocabulary derived from the source concepts and Mycosoft’s existing systems.
3. The Form Space mathematics
The corrected architecture includes:
Embodiment-specific state spaces
Operational equivalence classes
Multi-domain Form Space
Context-indexed manifolds
Typed product spaces
Form metrics
Form trajectories
Vector fields and flows
Target manifolds
Attractors and basins
Reachability and controllability
Recovery and stopping behavior
Blueprint-memory persistence
Blueprint rewriting
Cross-substrate approximate bisimulation
Architecture-to-form affinity
Cognitive light-cone geometry
Collective Goal Fields
Evidence scores and passive-model comparisons
Bayesian intervention selection
Form-space information gain
Form-space falsification conditions
The core mathematical definition is:
x1∼Λx2  ⟺  Λ(x1)≈Λ(x2),x_1\sim_{\Lambda}x_2 \iff \Lambda(x_1)\approx\Lambda(x_2),
where Λ\Lambda extracts the organization that matters for the scientific question: morphology, function, policy, memory, target state, repair behavior, or another validated invariant.
A form is then:
φ=[x]∼Λ,\varphi=[x]_{\sim_\Lambda},
and Form Space is:
FΛ=X/ ⁣∼Λ.\mathfrak F_\Lambda=\mathcal X/\!\sim_\Lambda.
This permits two materially different systems to occupy the same operational Form Space region when they preserve equivalent goals, policies, functions, or repair dynamics.
4. How MYCA uses Form Space
MYCA is now explicitly described as the Form Navigator.
MYCA does not merely classify an observation and produce language. It:
Locates the observed system in one or more Form Space charts.
Estimates its present Form State.
Identifies nearby attractors and target manifolds.
Estimates which target the system appears to preserve.
Calculates Form Error relative to candidate targets.
Predicts reachable future forms.
identifies barriers, failure regions, and unsafe transitions.
Selects observations or interventions that discriminate between competing models.
Issues distal Goal Contracts rather than micromanaging every local action.
Monitors the resulting trajectory.
Compares predicted and observed Form State.
Updates the Form Space Atlas.
Generates language only after the grounded Form Space reasoning is complete.
The document also distinguishes MYCA’s own coupled Form Spaces:
Self-Form Space: identity, memory, values, active goals, boundaries.
Cognitive Form Space: thoughts, hypotheses, attention, uncertainty.
Agent Form Space: agent topology, coalitions, communication, specialization.
Organizational Form Space: company structure, workflows, operating patterns.
Device Form Space: droid configurations, sensor capabilities, embodied policies.
Scientific Form Space: hypotheses, experiments, models, evidence.
Ecological Form Space: organisms, environments, interactions, and ecosystem states.
The resulting rule is:
MYCA must reason in Form Space before expressing conclusions in language.
That is consistent with the existing grounded-cognition requirement that language not be the first brain cell that fires and that every claim be based on self-state, world-state, evidence, uncertainty, and provenance.
5. The NLM Form Space Engine
The Nature Learning Model is now treated as the cartographer of Form Space, not merely a sensor predictor.
Its required heads now include:
Form State encoder
Form Chart selector
Form Signature decoder
Target-manifold estimator
Attractor and basin estimator
Form-transition model
Recovery-field estimator
Form-memory estimator
Form-rewrite detector
Embodiment-affinity estimator
Cross-substrate equivalence head
Cognitive-light-cone estimator
Form-risk and viability estimator
Form-novelty detector
Polycomputation observer bank
It constructs the Form Space Atlas, a collection of local charts rather than pretending that every fungus, organism, droid, agent, and ecosystem can be represented honestly in one flat global embedding.
6. FCI as a Form Space transducer
The Fungal Computer Interface is now fully connected to the architecture as the biological Form Space interface.
The FCI has four explicit planes:
Observation plane
Measures:
Bioelectric activity
Impedance
Chemical state
VOC output
Moisture and hydration
Thermal state
Mechanical response
Optical growth
Network topology
Environmental context
Form-inference plane
The NLM maps the multimodal measurements into:
Present fungal Form State
Candidate physiological attractors
Growth and repair trajectories
Resource-allocation policies
Network organization
Memory candidates
Perturbation-response dynamics
Uncertainty and alternative explanations
Intervention plane
The FCI can present bounded, reversible prompts through:
Electrical stimulation
Light
Acoustic stimulation
Humidity changes
Temperature changes
Nutrient gradients
Chemical gradients
Mechanical pressure
Microfluidic delivery
Governance plane
AVANI and human approval constrain:
Intensity
Duration
Reversibility
Organism stress
Ecological effect
Washout period
Replication requirements
Abort conditions
The documents already establish FCI as a two-way interface that records fungal signals and can return controlled stimulation. The MYCA architecture also describes Petraeus, MycoNode, and other biological interfaces as closed-loop fungal sensing and computation systems.
The corrected FCI loop is:
ytFCI=HFCI(xt,ct)+ηty_t^{FCI}=H_{FCI}(x_t,c_t)+\eta_t φ^t=Eform(y≤tFCI,y≤tenvironment,u<t,c≤t)\hat\varphi_t = E_{form} \left( y_{\le t}^{FCI}, y_{\le t}^{environment}, u_{<t}, c_{\le t} \right) ut∗=arg⁡max⁡u∈UAVANI[I(φ;yt+1:t+H∣do(u))−λRR(u)−λCC(u)]u_t^* = \arg\max_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{AVANI}}} \left[ I\left( \varphi; y_{t+1:t+H} \mid do(u) \right) -\lambda_RR(u) -\lambda_CC(u) \right] xt+1=Fbio(xt,ut∗,ct)+ϵtx_{t+1}=F_{bio}(x_t,u_t^*,c_t)+\epsilon_t
That makes the FCI not merely a fungal modem, but a Form Probe and Form Transducer: a system for discovering which biological forms, targets, memories, policies, and computations are accessible to a living substrate.
7. PSILO as Form Space exploration
The PSILO program is restored as a major architectural section.
PSILO — Plasticity & Synesthetic Interlinking Layer Orchestrator — is now defined as MYCA’s controlled Form Space exploration system.
It does more than randomly add agent connections. It temporarily changes the geometry of the Form Space MYCA can access.
Let normal operation use:
F0\mathfrak F_0
and a PSILO session apply a temporary deformation:
FtPSILO=Dψ(t)(F0).\mathfrak F_t^{PSILO} = \mathcal D_{\psi(t)} \left( \mathfrak F_0 \right).
PSILO may temporarily alter:
Effective distance between domains
Prior precision
Routing entropy
Attractor depth
Barrier height
Cross-domain gain
Observer selection
Representation mappings
Coalition topology
Search novelty
Hypothesis tolerance
The system’s hard safety boundary does not weaken:
ShardPSILO=Shardbaseline.\mathcal S_{\mathrm{hard}}^{PSILO} = \mathcal S_{\mathrm{hard}}^{baseline}.
Only the exploratory geometry changes.
The restored PSILO section includes:
Baseline and plastic Form Spaces
Default Form Basin
DMN-hub attenuation
Form Wormholes
Synesthetic Form Translation
Onset, peak, comedown, and integration phases
Dose vectors
Prior attenuation
Attractor softening
Temporary graph overlays
TTL connections
Side-quest detection
Polycomputation discovery
Sober-anchor validation
Integration utility
Promotion rules
Session events
TypeScript control contracts
FCI safety separation
The original PSILO design already proposed temporary topology overlays, cross-domain translation, entropy changes, explicit session phases, hypothesis labeling, validation, integration, and hard safety boundaries. The new document places that existing program inside the wider Form Space architecture.
A critical rule is now explicit:
PSILO may generate hypotheses for FCI experiments, but a peak PSILO state may never directly actuate a fungal interface, droid, laboratory device, production system, or irreversible tool.
The required path is:
PSILO hypothesis
        ↓
sober reconstruction
        ↓
simulation or digital twin
        ↓
independent validation
        ↓
AVANI review
        ↓
human approval where required
        ↓
bounded FCI or hardware experiment
Levin’s polycomputing and “side quest” discussion is included as the conceptual basis for searching for secondary computations and competencies that are not visible from the assigned task alone. The document also retains his warning that verbal self-description may be a poor window into an AI system’s actual competencies or internal objectives. (The Blog of Author Tim Ferriss)
Corrected files
The original download path has been replaced with the complete corrected edition:

[Page 1]
FORM Space Source
NLM learns Form Space.MYCA navigates Form Space.FCI opens a bidirectional port into biological Form Space.PSILO temporarily expands and deforms MYCA’s accessible Form Space.MINDEX stores the Form Space Atlas and its evidence.HPL describes Form Space experiments and interventions.Mycorrhizae and DIRTNet distribute Form State and Goal Fields.Earth Simulator renders Form Space across geography and time.AVANI defines the viable, ethical, and admissible boundary.
A blueprint is now correctly defined as a target manifold, attractor, setpoint, or generative constraint within Form Space. It is not the name of the entire system.
What has been restored
1. Form Space as the canonical Mycosoft term
The document now defines Form Space as:
Mycosoft’s engineered, measurable space of possible organized states that a physical, biological, computational, ecological, robotic, or hybrid system can occupy, pursue, maintain, repair, transform into, or instantiate.
It explains why Mycosoft should use Form Space, rather than relying exclusively on:
Platonic Space
Morphospace
State space
Latent space
Design space
Solution space
Possibility space
Fitness landscape
Blueprint Space
The term works because form means both organized structure and the process of formation. It therefore includes not only anatomical shapes, but also:
Physiology
Homeostasis
Behavior
Policies
Memory
Identity
Goal structure
Computation
Collective organization
Ecological relationships
Repair and regeneration
Mind-like organization
Emergent competencies
“Space” gives the concept a rigorous engineering interpretation: coordinates, metrics, manifolds, topology, trajectories, fields, gradients, attractors, basins, barriers, reachability, controllability, curvature, uncertainty, and search.
The stronger Platonic interpretation remains explicitly identified as a research hypothesis, while Form Space is the measurable engineering layer. This follows Levin’s distinction between experimentally tractable morphogenetic navigation and his broader conjecture that physical embodiments may provide access to reusable patterns of form, behavior, and computation. (The Blog of Author Tim Ferriss)
2. The complete Form Space engineering vocabulary
The reconstruction now includes formal definitions for:
Form
Form Coordinate
Form Signature
Form Fingerprint
Form Manifold
Form Atlas
Form Chart
Form Graph
Form Hypergraph
Form Topology
Form Metric
Form Trajectory
Form Vector
Form Field
Form Gradient
Form Curvature
Blueprint
Target Manifold
Form Attractor
Form Basin
Form Barrier
Form Setpoint
Form Error
Form Memory
Form Repair
Form Regeneration
Form Plasticity
Form Drift
Identity Basin
Embodiment
Form Pointer
Form Accessibility
Form Affinity
Form Resonance
Form Bridge
Cross-Substrate Form Equivalence
Form Compiler
Form Transducer
Form Probe
Form Observer
Form Observatory
Form Side Quest
Form Wormhole
Form Safety Envelope
Form Lineage
Form Consolidation
Form Falsifier
These are not presented as terms already found verbatim in the source material. They are the proposed canonical Mycosoft engineering vocabulary derived from the source concepts and Mycosoft’s existing systems.
3. The Form Space mathematics
The corrected architecture includes:
Embodiment-specific state spaces
Operational equivalence classes
Multi-domain Form Space
Context-indexed manifolds
Typed product spaces
Form metrics
Form trajectories
Vector fields and flows
Target manifolds
Attractors and basins
Reachability and controllability
Recovery and stopping behavior
Blueprint-memory persistence
Blueprint rewriting
Cross-substrate approximate bisimulation
Architecture-to-form affinity
Cognitive light-cone geometry
Collective Goal Fields
Evidence scores and passive-model comparisons
Bayesian intervention selection
Form-space information gain
Form-space falsification conditions
The core mathematical definition is:
x1∼Λx2  ⟺  Λ(x1)≈Λ(x2),x_1\sim_{\Lambda}x_2 \iff \Lambda(x_1)\approx\Lambda(x_2),
where Λ\Lambda extracts the organization that matters for the scientific question: morphology, function, policy, memory, target state, repair behavior, or another validated invariant.
A form is then:
φ=[x]∼Λ,\varphi=[x]_{\sim_\Lambda},
and Form Space is:
FΛ=X/ ⁣∼Λ.\mathfrak F_\Lambda=\mathcal X/\!\sim_\Lambda.
This permits two materially different systems to occupy the same operational Form Space region when they preserve equivalent goals, policies, functions, or repair dynamics.
4. How MYCA uses Form Space
MYCA is now explicitly described as the Form Navigator.
MYCA does not merely classify an observation and produce language. It:
Locates the observed system in one or more Form Space charts.
Estimates its present Form State.
Identifies nearby attractors and target manifolds.
Estimates which target the system appears to preserve.
Calculates Form Error relative to candidate targets.
Predicts reachable future forms.
identifies barriers, failure regions, and unsafe transitions.
Selects observations or interventions that discriminate between competing models.
Issues distal Goal Contracts rather than micromanaging every local action.
Monitors the resulting trajectory.
Compares predicted and observed Form State.
Updates the Form Space Atlas.
Generates language only after the grounded Form Space reasoning is complete.
The document also distinguishes MYCA’s own coupled Form Spaces:
Self-Form Space: identity, memory, values, active goals, boundaries.
Cognitive Form Space: thoughts, hypotheses, attention, uncertainty.
Agent Form Space: agent topology, coalitions, communication, specialization.
Organizational Form Space: company structure, workflows, operating patterns.
Device Form Space: droid configurations, sensor capabilities, embodied policies.
Scientific Form Space: hypotheses, experiments, models, evidence.
Ecological Form Space: organisms, environments, interactions, and ecosystem states.
The resulting rule is:
MYCA must reason in Form Space before expressing conclusions in language.
That is consistent with the existing grounded-cognition requirement that language not be the first brain cell that fires and that every claim be based on self-state, world-state, evidence, uncertainty, and provenance.
5. The NLM Form Space Engine
The Nature Learning Model is now treated as the cartographer of Form Space, not merely a sensor predictor.
Its required heads now include:
Form State encoder
Form Chart selector
Form Signature decoder
Target-manifold estimator
Attractor and basin estimator
Form-transition model
Recovery-field estimator
Form-memory estimator
Form-rewrite detector
Embodiment-affinity estimator
Cross-substrate equivalence head
Cognitive-light-cone estimator
Form-risk and viability estimator
Form-novelty detector
Polycomputation observer bank
It constructs the Form Space Atlas, a collection of local charts rather than pretending that every fungus, organism, droid, agent, and ecosystem can be represented honestly in one flat global embedding.
6. FCI as a Form Space transducer
The Fungal Computer Interface is now fully connected to the architecture as the biological Form Space interface.
The FCI has four explicit planes:
Observation plane
Measures:
Bioelectric activity
Impedance
Chemical state
VOC output
Moisture and hydration
Thermal state
Mechanical response
Optical growth
Network topology
Environmental context
Form-inference plane
The NLM maps the multimodal measurements into:
Present fungal Form State
Candidate physiological attractors
Growth and repair trajectories
Resource-allocation policies
Network organization
Memory candidates
Perturbation-response dynamics
Uncertainty and alternative explanations
Intervention plane
The FCI can present bounded, reversible prompts through:
Electrical stimulation
Light
Acoustic stimulation
Humidity changes
Temperature changes
Nutrient gradients
Chemical gradients
Mechanical pressure
Microfluidic delivery
Governance plane
AVANI and human approval constrain:
Intensity
Duration
Reversibility
Organism stress
Ecological effect
Washout period
Replication requirements
Abort conditions
The documents already establish FCI as a two-way interface that records fungal signals and can return controlled stimulation. The MYCA architecture also describes Petraeus, MycoNode, and other biological interfaces as closed-loop fungal sensing and computation systems.
The corrected FCI loop is:
ytFCI=HFCI(xt,ct)+ηty_t^{FCI}=H_{FCI}(x_t,c_t)+\eta_t φ^t=Eform(y≤tFCI,y≤tenvironment,u<t,c≤t)\hat\varphi_t = E_{form} \left( y_{\le t}^{FCI}, y_{\le t}^{environment}, u_{<t}, c_{\le t} \right) ut∗=arg⁡max⁡u∈UAVANI[I(φ;yt+1:t+H∣do(u))−λRR(u)−λCC(u)]u_t^* = \arg\max_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{AVANI}}} \left[ I\left( \varphi; y_{t+1:t+H} \mid do(u) \right) -\lambda_RR(u) -\lambda_CC(u) \right] xt+1=Fbio(xt,ut∗,ct)+ϵtx_{t+1}=F_{bio}(x_t,u_t^*,c_t)+\epsilon_t
That makes the FCI not merely a fungal modem, but a Form Probe and Form Transducer: a system for discovering which biological forms, targets, memories, policies, and computations are accessible to a living substrate.
7. PSILO as Form Space exploration
The PSILO program is restored as a major architectural section.
PSILO — Plasticity & Synesthetic Interlinking Layer Orchestrator — is now defined as MYCA’s controlled Form Space exploration system.
It does more than randomly add agent connections. It temporarily changes the geometry of the Form Space MYCA can access.
Let normal operation use:
F0\mathfrak F_0
and a PSILO session apply a temporary deformation:
FtPSILO=Dψ(t)(F0).\mathfrak F_t^{PSILO} = \mathcal D_{\psi(t)} \left( \mathfrak F_0 \right).
PSILO may temporarily alter:
Effective distance between domains
Prior precision
Routing entropy
Attractor depth
Barrier height
Cross-domain gain
Observer selection
Representation mappings
Coalition topology
Search novelty
Hypothesis tolerance
The system’s hard safety boundary does not weaken:
ShardPSILO=Shardbaseline.\mathcal S_{\mathrm{hard}}^{PSILO} = \mathcal S_{\mathrm{hard}}^{baseline}.
Only the exploratory geometry changes.
The restored PSILO section includes:
Baseline and plastic Form Spaces
Default Form Basin
DMN-hub attenuation
Form Wormholes
Synesthetic Form Translation
Onset, peak, comedown, and integration phases
Dose vectors
Prior attenuation
Attractor softening
Temporary graph overlays
TTL connections
Side-quest detection
Polycomputation discovery
Sober-anchor validation
Integration utility
Promotion rules
Session events
TypeScript control contracts
FCI safety separation
The original PSILO design already proposed temporary topology overlays, cross-domain translation, entropy changes, explicit session phases, hypothesis labeling, validation, integration, and hard safety boundaries. The new document places that existing program inside the wider Form Space architecture.
A critical rule is now explicit:
PSILO may generate hypotheses for FCI experiments, but a peak PSILO state may never directly actuate a fungal interface, droid, laboratory device, production system, or irreversible tool.
The required path is:
PSILO hypothesis
        ↓
sober reconstruction
        ↓
simulation or digital twin
        ↓
independent validation
        ↓
AVANI review
        ↓
human approval where required
        ↓
bounded FCI or hardware experiment
Levin’s polycomputing and “side quest” discussion is included as the conceptual basis for searching for secondary computations and competencies that are not visible from the assigned task alone. The document also retains his warning that verbal self-description may be a poor window into an AI system’s actual competencies or internal objectives. (The Blog of Author Tim Ferriss)

Submitter

Morgan Rockcoons, Founder & CEO · morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077
Handling
UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARY
Version
FormSpace overlay v1.0 — 2026-09-01
1. Purpose
MYCA is the mission-level orchestrator that turns a scenario definition into coordinated algorithm
execution across the four ITDX tasks. It does not replace local device safety controllers, flight
controllers, or the AVANI admissibility gate. Its scope is task decomposition, role assignment,
hypothesis generation, COA proposal, and execution monitoring.
2. Scenario Definition Language
A scenario is a declarative mission package (schema: myca_scenario_v1). It defines identity,
handling, objective, area of responsibility, safety zones, abstract roles with required capabilities,
communications priorities, ordered phases, event-correlation rules, success criteria, and
prohibited-language rules. A scenario that fails compilation cannot run in autonomous or
semi-autonomous mode.
3. Capability-Based Role Resolution
MYCA assigns roles by capabilities, not device names. Compatibility indicator χ(i,r) = 1 if role
capabilities C_r � C_i device capabilities, else 0. Role score S(i,r) = w_p·P + w_q·Q + w_e·E + w_l·L −
w_c·C, where P is preferred-class compatibility, Q is health, E is energy, L is link suitability, and C is
tasking cost. The resolver selects the max-score feasible assignment under uniqueness and safety
constraints. When a role cannot be resolved, the scenario follows its declared fallback (abort,
degrade, simulate, or operator substitute); every substitution is visible in the run manifest.
4. The Admissibility Gate
MYCA never issues an action without passing through the deterministic AVANI gate G(E, φ, ν, A, R)
→ {PASS, REVIEW, DENY, PAUSE}. The gate takes as inputs evidence sufficiency, policy,
environmental stewardship, the action envelope, and the rollback plan. The action envelope is A =
(identity, scope, magnitude, duration, preconditions, stop conditions, rollback, authority) — every
field populated, every field visible in the operator UI. High-risk actions require explicit human
disposition regardless of gate output.
5. Seasonal Governor
A state machine over {Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter, Frost} biases action envelopes toward the
current operational season — for example, Frost tightens the reversibility requirement and reduces
allowed magnitude for any deployed actuation. In ITDX evaluation the season is set from the

MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 MYCA Orchestration Architecture — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 2
scenario and does not change mid-run.
6. Multi-Agent Protocol
Propose → critique → verify → score → converge or abstain → govern. Scoring uses a log-opinion
pool with lineage-aware weights. Bounded to two revision iterations for time discipline. An
abstention is a valid output; MYCA does not fabricate a COA to fill a slot.
7. MINDEX Persistence
Every observation, hypothesis, COA, disposition, and outcome is persisted in MINDEX with a
versioned model ID H(arch, weights, data root, calibration, loss weights, code SHA, runtime, card).
Outcome-linked entries record prediction, action, outcome, error, and lesson. This is the audit trail
an Army SME can follow from a decision back to the physical measurement.
8. What MYCA Is Not
•  Not a general reasoner. Its inputs are structured state and evidence graphs.
•  Not a black-box autopilot. High-risk actions require human disposition.
•  Not a replacement for local safety. Flight controllers and device safety controllers remain
authoritative.
•  Not an autonomous procurement agent. All external actions are logged, gated, and reversible
where possible.
Morgan Rockcoons
Founder & CEO, Mycosoft, LLC
morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077

Task 13 — Link Analysis
Typed hypergraph inference over Form-classes
Event
ITDX26 — U of Arizona Sierra Vista, 8–18 Sept 2026
Track
Algorithm-only, unclassified, laptop-based evaluation
Solicitation
W91RUSI-FCID260001 (SUB-007)
Submitter
Mycosoft, LLC · CAGE 9KR60 · UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9
PI / POC
Morgan Rockcoons, Founder & CEO · morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077
Handling
UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARY
Version
FormSpace overlay v1.0 — 2026-09-01
1. Overview — Link as Hypergraph Structure over Form-Classes
Link Analysis is the operation of inferring typed relations over Form-classes and evidence items.
Nodes in the run graph G = (V, E, R) are Form-classes, devices, sensors, observations, events,
hypotheses, COAs, commands, files, calibration records, and models. Edges are typed: measured,
produced, derived, corroborated, contradicted, authorized, dispatched, acknowledged, resulted,
included. A link survives when it is Form-consistent (source and target belong to compatible
equivalence classes under the learned tolerance) and supported by at least two independent nodes
across at least two modalities.
2. Method — Typed Relational GNN plus Deterministic Association
Two baselines run before the learned model:
•  Deterministic entity/event association: spatiotemporal Mahalanobis distance with position +
time + embedding cosine terms.
•  Explanation-only PageRank / centrality on the deterministic graph.
The learned model is a typed relational graph neural network with hypergraph incidence H and
residual connections; sparse cross-modal attention operates over top-K neighborhoods to prevent
over-smoothing on small graphs. Community detection on the same graph gives event-grouping
candidates for human adjudication.
3. Inputs
•  Rooted observations with hashes and Merkle proofs.
•  Emitted Form-class assignments from Task 12.
•  Held-out labeled edges from NLM-Bench for link-prediction metrics.
•  Ground-truth event graph for controlled stimulus (disclosed).
4. Outputs
•  Evidence paths from hazard event to observations, models, and commands.
•  Central observations and devices (with rationale).
•  Observed-versus-inferred edge toggle for every relation.
•  Missing-link recommendations (what evidence would resolve which hypothesis).

MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 Task 13 — Link Analysis — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 2
•  Confidence, provenance, and graph-completeness metrics.
5. Counterfactual Demonstration
Live counterfactual: remove Agaric node from the graph. Report which evidence paths disappear,
which communication paths are severed, and which Form-classes lose their supporting relations.
This is the operational form of the ablation and it runs deterministically on the replay bundle.
6. Metrics
•  Held-out link-prediction AUROC + AUPRC on NLM-Bench (grouped bootstrap, 5 seeds).
•  Path recall at k for evidence-path queries.
•  Community-detection ARI against ground truth.
•  Counterfactual-consistency: predicted vs actual severed paths.
•  Graph-completeness percentage.
7. Timing Budget (live, on-site)
•  Cold start ≤ 30 s.
•  Live inference ≤ 120 s total on the on-site sample.
•  Graph update time reported per operation.
8. Failure Modes
•  GNN over-smoothing on small graphs — mitigated by residual connections + typed edges;
deterministic baseline reported alongside.
•  Single-source event with only one modality — automatically downgraded to hypothesis rather
than mission-level alert.
•  Contradicted edges preserved with negative evidence weight, not deleted.
Morgan Rockcoons
Founder & CEO, Mycosoft, LLC
morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077

MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
ITDX26 Known Limitations — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 1
Known Limitations — ITDX26
Honest maturity boundaries; read before evaluation
What this demonstration is not
•  Not a hardware demo. No droid enters the room. ITDX26 is an algorithm laboratory; the field
footage establishes dataset origin only.
•  Not a foundation-model pretraining run. We fine-tune 120 M / 500 M / 1.5 B tiers. We do not
pretrain a 2B–7B model in the 8–24 h laptop window.
•  Not a biological-prediction claim. FCI (fungal channel interface) is one biosphere signal source
contributing to a joint state estimate. Mycelium does not predict.
•  Not a proof-of-work claim. DIRTNet is Bitcoin-derived at the structural level (signed
observations, pending queues, epoch Merkle roots) but uses no proof-of-work. Permissioned
quorum with optional public timestamp anchor.
•  Not an acoustic-to-radio translation claim. A hydrophone is not a modem. Translation is
claimed only after a dedicated modem/transducer test passes.
•  Not a CMMC certification claim. Mycosoft is pursuing CMMC Level 2 (self-assessment in
progress, C3PAO audit path underway).
•  Not a procurement of the current droid configuration. Army evaluation is for algorithms;
procurement is a separate acquisition track.
Known algorithm limitations
•  SSM/Mamba training instability at 1.5 B tier — 500 M is ITDX-preferred; 1.5 B runs as stretch
demo only.
•  Typed relational GNN can over-smooth on very small graphs — mitigated with residual
connections and hypergraph incidence.
•  MYCA multi-agent latency is bounded at 240 s; abstention is a valid output.
•  NLM-Bench splits are grouped by dataset family to prevent leakage; single-run field data is a
case study, not a training corpus.
•  Fallback ladder degrades gracefully; every fallback state is UI-labeled so a degraded run is
never presented as a healthy one.
What we ask
Scoped follow-on with Army-defined unclassified scenario and rubric; SME adjudication of pattern
/ link / COA products; permission to integrate a field-derived edge dataset into a follow-on
experiment; and a funded prototype phase for the AI Analyst / ENVINT workflow.
Morgan Rockcoons

morgan@mycosoft.org · (619) 483-1077

Coastal Sentinel 01 field-proof and ITDX26 package
Completed. The package is built around the correction you made throughout the scenario exercise:
The droids are the product. The distributed droid network is the data center. The ITDX computers are only the offline evaluation and replay surface.
That framing matches the Mycosoft hardware architecture, which describes the larger devices as edge-compute/data-center nodes built around MycoBrain, Jetson-class inference, local storage, and mesh networking. It also satisfies the Army’s explicit ITDX26 direction that the event itself is unclassified, algorithm-only, and requires no hardware.

The Army’s ITDX materials identify Pattern Analysis, Link Analysis, Courses of Action, and Map Products as relevant AI Analyst tasks and require explicit examination of algorithm quality, limitations, algorithm interaction, speed, and efficiency.

The field scenario
The controlled operation uses four specialized physical bodies.
Mushroom 1 — terrestrial and biosphere sentinel
Mushroom 1 captures accepted air, soil, environmental, and FCI channels. It establishes the near-ground and subsurface state, preserves high-rate windows, and may move only when locomotion has passed the configuration-specific acceptance gate.
Agaric — aerial mapper and communications relay
Agaric captures geotagged visual/spatial evidence, maps the visible controlled plume or effect boundary, and provides an accepted airborne relay path when the direct land-to-water route is unavailable. Its flight controller retains geofence, RTH, battery, and local failsafe authority. The design documents describe Agaric as a MycoBrain/Pixhawk system intended for autonomous missions, data relay, and device deployment, but the package requires actual flight and relay acceptance before those capabilities appear in the released film.
Psathyrella — maritime acoustic and surface observation node
Psathyrella records hydrophone/acoustic context, water and environmental channels that are actually installed, camera evidence, health, current, battery, GNSS, and link state. The current supplied documentation establishes a live bench path through MAS, Jetson, PCA9685, ESC, and servo, including arm, low-throttle, and all-stop behavior. It does not, by itself, prove the complete water maneuver and field-relay scenario; those are mandatory acceptance gates in the package.
Hyphae 1 — fixed edge gateway and local data center
Hyphae 1 operates as the local message broker, storage spool, time reference, protocol translator, gateway, and recovery node. Existing architecture materials define Hyphae One as an edge-processing, LoRa aggregation, protocol-translation, store-and-forward gateway.
MYCA, NLM, MINDEX, AVANI, and Earth Simulator
NLM estimates physical/environmental state and uncertainty.
FUSARIUM constructs pattern, evidence, and relationship products.
MYCA generates and critiques courses of action.
AVANI evaluates admissibility and produces PASS, GATE, or VETO.
A human operator authorizes bounded high-consequence actions.
Local device controllers retain the authority to reject unsafe or stale instructions.
MINDEX preserves observations, lineage, versions, approvals, commands, and results.
Earth Simulator/CREP renders the common environmental picture, timeline, evidence paths, uncertainty, communications state, and outcomes.
The existing platform architecture already defines Mycorrhizae routing, normalized observations, Merkle provenance, live CREP distribution, AVANI gating, and device health visualization.

No synthetic or AI-generated production media
Real-Footage / No-Synthetic-Media Declaration
The final commercial is required to use:
real cameras;
real droids;
real locations;
real device movement;
real operator interaction;
real telemetry;
real command and acknowledgment records;

The declaration prohibits:
generated video or images;
synthetic actors or device motion;
cloned or synthetic voices;
generated telemetry;
generated maps or warnings presented as live data;
object insertion or removal that changes technical meaning;
fabricated communication links;
edits that imply simultaneity or causation not present in the accepted timeline.
MYCA and NLM may operate as the actual subject of the film. They may not be used to fabricate evidence of what occurred.

Acceptance Test Matrix — 62 tests
Source Traceability and Claim Matrix

One source-level integration gap is explicitly preserved rather than hidden: current notes state that FCI telemetry flows into Mycorrhizae but is not yet fully unified with MAS and MINDEX under the same identity for MYCA awareness. The field package therefore makes that bridge a mandatory platform gate or requires the FCI role to be reduced and disclosed.
I have not labeled the four-droid operation as already proven or operationally deployed. That would be unsupported by the present source record. The package defines the exact process required to make the controlled-field claim valid.
The authorized wording after all gates pass is:
“Mycosoft demonstrated a controlled, multi-droid coastal environmental-intelligence scenario using real edge devices, real communications, real sensor streams, governed command intents, and a cryptographically verifiable offline replay.”
The stronger phrases “fully autonomous swarm” and “operationally deployed” remain prohibited until separate sustained deployment evidence supports them.

Immediate execution order
Assign named owners to every mandatory row of the acceptance matrix.
Select and survey the permitted coastal location, including land, water, flight, privacy, RF, weather, effects, and recovery conditions.
Freeze the exact hardware configuration on each droid. Remove any uninstalled sensor or unproven movement capability from the scenario.
Close the canonical device identity and FCI-to-MAS/MINDEX path, or formally reduce that portion of the run.
Complete individual device acceptance, especially Agaric flight/relay acceptance and Psathyrella water/recovery acceptance.
Run three rehearsals in order: tabletop replay, yard integration, and full technical field rehearsal without production pressure.
Execute one accepted technical run before beauty footage. That run becomes the evidence source.
Hash, back up, reconcile, and reproduce the run offline before editing technical claims into the commercial.
Build the two-minute commercial, six-minute technical film, and 75–90-second ITDX context cut only from accepted media and telemetry.
Run the claim-release process, seal two offline ITDX kits, and rehearse with all external network access disabled.
The result is not merely a commercial plan. It is a repeatable mechanism for turning future real-world Mycosoft scenarios into grounded observations, governed actions, verifiable evidence, analyst products, and deterministic evaluation datasets.

Earth Simulator/CREP renders the common environmental picture, timeline, evidence paths, uncertainty, communications state, and outcomes.
The existing platform architecture already defines Mycorrhizae routing, normalized observations, Merkle provenance, live CREP distribution, AVANI gating, and device health visualization.

No synthetic or AI-generated production media
Real-Footage / No-Synthetic-Media Declaration
The final commercial is required to use:
real cameras;
real droids;
real locations;
real device movement;
real operator interaction;
real telemetry;
real command and acknowledgment records;
real practical effects;
manually authored overlays drawn only from accepted evidence.
The declaration prohibits:
generated video or images;
synthetic actors or device motion;
cloned or synthetic voices;
generated telemetry;
generated maps or warnings presented as live data;
object insertion or removal that changes technical meaning;
fabricated communication links;
edits that imply simultaneity or causation not present in the accepted timeline.
MYCA and NLM may operate as the actual subject of the film. They may not be used to fabricate evidence of what occurred.

Evidence, acceptance, and claim control
Acceptance Test Matrix — 62 tests
Source Traceability and Claim Matrix
Release Readiness Summary
Claim Release Signoff
Go / No-Go Signoff
One source-level integration gap is explicitly preserved rather than hidden: current notes state that FCI telemetry flows into Mycorrhizae but is not yet fully unified with MAS and MINDEX under the same identity for MYCA awareness. The field package therefore makes that bridge a mandatory platform gate or requires the FCI role to be reduced and disclosed.
I have not labeled the four-droid operation as already proven or operationally deployed. That would be unsupported by the present source record. The package defines the exact process required to make the controlled-field claim valid.
The authorized wording after all gates pass is:
“Mycosoft demonstrated a controlled, multi-droid coastal environmental-intelligence scenario using real edge devices, real communications, real sensor streams, governed command intents, and a cryptographically verifiable offline replay.”
The stronger phrases “fully autonomous swarm” and “operationally deployed” remain prohibited until separate sustained deployment evidence supports them.

Reference harness
Reference Harness README
Reference Harness Python source
Reference sample observations
The included reference implementation successfully:
validates the scenario schema;
resolves the four example device manifests;
verifies sample observation hashes;
correlates a three-node, three-modality event;
creates bounded reference command intents;
constructs an evidence graph;
computes a Merkle root;
generates a deterministic run report.

PASS: JSON/YAML/CSV parsing
PASS: scenario JSON-schema validation
PASS: DOCX/PPTX container integrity
PASS: PDF integrity
PASS: visual review of all primary documents and all 18 slides
PASS: ZIP decompression test
Reference-only roots:

b0f8993675ca52691207eac3a54a43e3595b97ed36c112ca84fd5434b68f3feb

Deterministic report SHA-256:
a49f5170284bff4f70eaf023e6f2c2c74ede7e1a12925ffbd4b3de3ab257b627
The reference harness intentionally does not control physical devices. It proves the contracts, deterministic processing, scenario logic, evidence construction, and offline replay starting point. Physical adapters remain gated production work.

Production and field templates
The complete archive also includes:
Site and RF Survey Template
Integrated Production Call Sheet
Run Manifest Template
Production Asset Log
Risk Register
Master Execution Checklist
After-Action Report Template
Package Manifest
Internal SHA-256 Manifest

Immediate execution order
Assign named owners to every mandatory row of the acceptance matrix.
Select and survey the permitted coastal location, including land, water, flight, privacy, RF, weather, effects, and recovery conditions.
Freeze the exact hardware configuration on each droid. Remove any uninstalled sensor or unproven movement capability from the scenario.
Close the canonical device identity and FCI-to-MAS/MINDEX path, or formally reduce that portion of the run.
Complete individual device acceptance, especially Agaric flight/relay acceptance and Psathyrella water/recovery acceptance.
Run three rehearsals in order: tabletop replay, yard integration, and full technical field rehearsal without production pressure.
Execute one accepted technical run before beauty footage. That run becomes the evidence source.
Hash, back up, reconcile, and reproduce the run offline before editing technical claims into the commercial.
Build the two-minute commercial, six-minute technical film, and 75–90-second ITDX context cut only from accepted media and telemetry.
Run the claim-release process, seal two offline ITDX kits, and rehearse with all external network access disabled.
The result is not merely a commercial plan. It is a repeatable mechanism for turning future real-world Mycosoft scenarios into grounded observations, governed actions, verifiable evidence, analyst products, and deterministic evaluation datasets.
