Task 8 requires at least 18/20 because generative risk is higher. ## 13.9 8 August deliverable checklist ### Scope and naming - [ ] Every system-name occurrence uses **MYCA** exactly. - [ ] NLM means Nature Learning Model. - [ ] No required hardware appears in the ITDX26 demo path. - [ ] All content is UNCLASSIFIED and public-data based. - [ ] Mycosoft is described as self-performing the demonstration. - [ ] Every performance number is labeled target, budget, or measured. ### Science and mathematics - [ ] State-space, graph, MYCA, and AVANI formalism reviewed. - [ ] Composite losses and inference equations have defined variables. - [ ] Deterministic and stochastic rails are separated. - [ ] Calibration and uncertainty methods are specified. - [ ] Falsification conditions are stated. - [ ] Algorithm baselines receive equal mathematical treatment. ### Data - [ ] Dataset admission predicate and manifest schema approved. - [ ] ACLED default exclusion implemented. - [ ] GDELT article-body restriction respected. - [ ] OSM attribution and ODbL record prepared. - [ ] OGB dataset and official evaluator selected. - [ ] Wikidata QID/entity split specified. - [ ] Common Crawl is absent or metadata/rights-filtered. - [ ] Doctrine index and public-release records included. ### Engineering - [ ] Repository tree exists. - [ ] Candidate dependency locks install offline. - [ ] NMF/task/run-report schemas compile. - [ ] Seed and determinism initializer implemented. - [ ] `make doctor`, `make demo`, and `make verify-package` interfaces exist. - [ ] Unit/integration/determinism test inventory assigned. - [ ] Both machine profiles have a qualification plan. ### Evaluation - [ ] Five seeds preregistered. - [ ] Primary and guardrail metrics fixed. - [ ] Paired test and bootstrap unit fixed. - [ ] Minimum operational effects fixed. - [ ] Human-rating rubric fixed where needed. - [ ] Pareto measurement protocol fixed. - [ ] Underperformance script rehearsable. ### Presentation - [ ] Architecture figures numbered and sourced. - [ ] Each task has a one-page analyst product mockup. - [ ] Live/prerecorded/static state is visible. - [ ] Evidence, uncertainty, governance, and performance appear together. - [ ] Calendar uses the correct 2026 weekdays. - [ ] No unsupported marketing superlative appears as a measured claim. ## 13.10 Definition of done for the design phase The 8 August design phase is done when a competent engineer who did not author the plan can answer, without oral clarification: 1. what exact data enter each task; 2. what mathematical transformation occurs; 3. what structured object comes out; 4. how it is calibrated and governed; 5. which baseline is run on the same data; 6. how success and failure are measured; 7. how the task fails safely; 8. how to run it offline; 9. how to reproduce it from hashes and locks; 10. what the September demonstration may and may not claim. If any answer depends on “Morgan will explain it live,” the design is incomplete. --- # Part 9 — DIRTNet decentralized-edge algorithm study # 14. DIRTNet algorithm-only demonstration ## 14.1 Purpose and Army-facing relevance DIRTNet is a cross-cutting experiment, not a fifth doctrinal task. It addresses the four ICED assessment elements directly: 1. whether local and federated algorithms preserve Task 12/13 quality; 2. where partitions, bandwidth constraints, stale models, and compromised nodes cause failure; 3. how NLM, graph analytics, MYCA, AVANI, MINDEX, and transport algorithms interact; 4. how much latency, memory, network traffic, and availability change under decentralized execution. The demonstration thesis is: > An AI-analyst architecture should not require every raw observation to traverse a reliable broadband link before becoming useful. Edge nodes can produce calibrated, signed, compact analytic objects locally, remain useful during disconnection, and later converge through cryptographically verifiable synchronization. ![Figure 18. DIRTNet virtual-edge emulator for ITDX26.](graphics/fig18_itdx_dirtnet_algorithm_emulator.png) ## 14.2 Virtual-node topology The reference topology uses four local processes or containers: | Virtual node | Local data and algorithm | Primary output | |---|---|---| | `edge-pattern-a` | northern or early-time event shard; Task 12 small SSM | anomaly events, temporal embeddings, local patterns | | `edge-link-b` | southern or graph shard; Task 13 small GNN | entities, links, communities, link uncertainty | | `edge-sensing-c` | replayed BlueSight/SINE/GANDHA/FCI feature windows | multimodal events and evidence handles | | `field-gateway` | Mycorrhizae, MINDEX checkpoint, AVANI edge policy, anti-entropy | reconciled evidence graph and federated checkpoint | MYCA operates as a distributed analyst over the node outputs. FUSARIUM/CREP renders the network state, patterns, links, map layers, and audit objects. ## 14.3 Transport emulator Each directed link has profile \[ \lambda_{ij}=(R_{ij},L_{ij},p_{ij},d_{ij},h_{ij},c_{ij}), \] where \(R\) is bitrate, \(L\) delay, \(p\) loss, \(d\) duty-cycle budget, \(h\) hop limit, and \(c\) cost. The emulator enforces queueing, delay, loss, fragmentation, retry, and partition schedules. Recommended nominal profiles are stored in `dirtnet_itdx26_emulator_example.yaml`. They are controlled abstractions, not claims of exact radio-channel fidelity. ### Required profiles - LoRa-like low-rate, low-duty-cycle direct link; - LoRaWAN-like gateway path with uplink scheduling; - Meshtastic-like low-rate, multi-hop mesh; - Wi-Fi/Ethernet high-bandwidth sync contact; - complete partition; - asymmetric link and delayed acknowledgment. ## 14.4 Signed message and identity contract The DIRTNet message must validate: 1. schema/version; 2. node identity and key status; 3. sequence and replay window; 4. content hash; 5. signature; 6. time and uncertainty; 7. calibration and quality; 8. routing TTL/hop constraints; 9. data scope/classification; 10. prior hash and epoch reference. A dedupe identity is \[ d(m)=H(node\_id\Vert sequence\Vert content\_hash). \] Repeated delivery refreshes acknowledgment state but cannot create a duplicate observation. ## 14.5 Merkle checkpoint and anti-entropy algorithm Each node batches ordered record hashes into an epoch tree and publishes a signed root. The gateway forms \[ R_e=H(e\Vert R_{e-1}\Vert MerkleRoot(H(i_1\Vert R_{i_1,e}),\ldots,H(i_q\Vert R_{i_q,e}))\Vert H(\Pi_e)). \] Synchronization proceeds: ```text exchange signed manifests -> compare node/stream epoch ranges and roots -> if root equal: acknowledge, no payload transfer -> if root differs: descend Merkle ranges or request missing sequence ranges -> verify content hash and node signature -> reject replay/forgery/stale command -> merge immutable records by identity -> retain explicit branches/conflicts -> create new federated checkpoint ``` The expected reconciliation transfer for sparse differences is substantially smaller than full log transfer. The measured metric is bytes transferred to reach an identical admissible record set. ![Figure 12. DIRTNet cryptographic provenance and Bitcoin-derived mapping.](graphics/fig12_dirtnet_cryptographic_provenance.png) ## 14.6 Bandwidth-aware event selection Each queued object receives score \[ S_m=\frac{\alpha U_m+\beta V_m+\gamma N_m+\delta Q_m+\epsilon F_m+\zeta D_m} {b_m+\lambda_a a_m+\lambda_e e_m}, \] where \(b_m\) is bytes, \(a_m\) airtime, \(e_m\) energy proxy, and the numerator represents urgency, decision value, novelty, quality, freshness, and evidence diversity. Under a constrained contact budget \(B\), choose \[ \max_{x_m\in\{0,1\}}\sum_m x_m(\alpha U_m+\beta V_m+\gamma N_m+\delta Q_m+\epsilon F_m+\zeta D_m) \] subject to \[ \sum_m x_m b_m\le B, \] with hard inclusion for mandatory critical alerts and governance records. This becomes a knapsack or online scheduling problem with age and expiry. ## 14.7 Decentralized Task 12 Each pattern node runs the Task 12 streaming recurrence on a local shard. It publishes: - compact event embedding; - calibrated anomaly score; - changepoint score; - candidate cluster summary; - evidence quality and source diversity; - content address for selected raw records; - signed local epoch root. The gateway performs global candidate fusion without requiring all raw events: \[ A(C)=\sum_i w_iA_i(C_i)+\lambda_{cross}\sum_{i/ run_report.json node_manifests/ signed_messages/ sync_manifests/ epoch_checkpoints/ merkle_proofs/ network_trace.parquet queue_trace.parquet model_inventory.json task12_metrics.json task13_metrics.json coa_metrics.json failure_audit.json rendered_network.png rendered_crep_product.png ``` ## 14.18 Scope boundary The emulator demonstrates algorithms for distributed edge coordination. It does not prove RF performance, field durability, sensor calibration, battery endurance, secure-element resistance, biological semantic decoding, or operational military suitability. Those require hardware and field trials outside ITDX26. --- # 15. Reference register ## 15.1 Scope and doctrine - **[D1]** U.S. Army, ITDX26 Special Notice, solicitation **W91RUSI-FCID260001**, including the 16 focus-area intelligence tasks and four essential elements of analysis. Public SAM.gov opportunity record archived in the package. - **[D2]** U.S. Department of the Army, **ATP 2-33.4, Intelligence Analysis**, public release used for analytic techniques including pattern and link analysis. - **[D3]** U.S. Department of the Army, **FM 2-0, Intelligence**, public release used for intelligence-process and product context. - **[D4]** U.S. Department of the Army, **ATP 2-01.3, Intelligence Preparation of the Operational Environment**, public release used for geospatial and operational-environment products. - **[D5]** U.S. Department of the Army, **ATP 2-01, Plan Requirements and Assess Collection**, public release used for collection-planning context. - **[D6]** U.S. Department of the Army, **FM 5-0, Planning and Orders Production**, public release used for course-of-action development and FASDC screening. - **[D7]** Joint Chiefs of Staff, **JP 2-0, Joint Intelligence**, public release used for joint intelligence context. - **[SCOPE1]** Mycosoft, `00_BINDER_ITDX26_ChatGPT_Handoff.md`, 16 July 2026. - **[SCOPE2]** Mycosoft, `02_action_plan.md`, 16 July 2026. - **[SCOPE3]** Mycosoft, `03_sources_framework.md`, 16 July 2026. - **[SCOPE4]** Mycosoft, `04_time_schedule.md`, corrected in this plan to the actual September 2026 weekdays. - **[SCOPE5]** Mycosoft, `05_proposal_what_we_demonstrate.md`, 16 July 2026. - **[SCOPE6]** Mycosoft, `06_chatgpt_handoff_prompt.md`, 16 July 2026. ## 15.2 Mathematical and algorithmic references - **[M1]** Albert Gu and Tri Dao, “Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces,” arXiv:2312.00752, 2023. - **[M2]** Tri Dao and Albert Gu, “Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality,” arXiv:2405.21060, 2024. - **[M3]** William L. Hamilton, Rex Ying, and Jure Leskovec, “Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs,” NeurIPS, 2017. - **[M4]** Petar Veličković et al., “Graph Attention Networks,” ICLR, 2018. - **[M5]** Aditya Grover and Jure Leskovec, “node2vec: Scalable Feature Learning for Networks,” KDD, 2016. - **[M6]** Vincent D. Blondel et al., “Fast Unfolding of Communities in Large Networks,” Journal of Statistical Mechanics, 2008. - **[M7]** Lawrence Page, Sergey Brin, Rajeev Motwani, and Terry Winograd, “The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web,” Stanford technical report, 1999. - **[M8]** Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, *A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction*, Journal of Machine Learning Research, 2008; and current implementation guidance archived with the code. - **[M9]** Aaron van den Oord, Yazhe Li, and Oriol Vinyals, “Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding,” arXiv:1807.03748, 2018. - **[M10]** Michael Schlichtkrull et al., “Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks,” ESWC, 2018. - **[M11]** Chuan Guo et al., “On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks,” ICML, 2017. - **[M12]** Glenn W. Brier, “Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability,” Monthly Weather Review, 1950. - **[M13]** Leo Breiman, “Random Forests,” Machine Learning, 2001, where used as a classical tabular comparator. - **[M14]** Yarin Gal and Zoubin Ghahramani, “Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation,” ICML, 2016, where stochastic dropout uncertainty is evaluated. - **[M15]** Satoshi Nakamoto, “Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System,” 2008. Used only for peer-node, signature, hash-chain, Merkle-tree, best-effort-network, and compact-proof design patterns; routine DIRTNet does not use proof-of-work. - **[M16]** NVIDIA, “Japan's Robotics and Manufacturing Leaders Build on NVIDIA Cosmos to Advance Physical AI Frontier,” 15 July 2026. - **[M17]** NVIDIA, “Japan Government, Industrial Leaders and NVIDIA Launch the World's First National AI Infrastructure,” 16 July 2026. ## 15.3 Dataset and licensing references - **[DATA1]** GDELT Project, GDELT 2.1 event data and documentation, https://www.gdeltproject.org/. Current terms and acquisition receipt archived per dataset manifest. - **[DATA2]** Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, current Terms of Use and licensing materials, https://acleddata.com/terms-of-use/. Excluded from the default package unless written authorization is archived. - **[DATA3]** OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License and copyright/attribution guidance, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright. - **[DATA4]** U.S. Geological Survey data and product metadata, https://www.usgs.gov/; product-specific notices control. - **[DATA5]** NASA Earthdata, data-use and citation guidance plus product-specific metadata, https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/. - **[DATA6]** Stanford Network Analysis Project datasets, https://snap.stanford.edu/data/; individual dataset terms control. - **[DATA7]** Weihua Hu et al., “Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs,” NeurIPS, 2020; official data and evaluator at https://ogb.stanford.edu/. - **[DATA8]** Wikidata, CC0 public-domain dedication and frozen dump metadata, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing. - **[DATA9]** Common Crawl terms and data documentation, https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use; underlying content rights remain source-specific. - **[DATA10]** Public U.S. Army/Joint doctrine and public training exemplars admitted through package records. - **[DATA11]** Mycosoft, `NLM_Training_Data_Catalog.pdf`, April/July 2026 versions; dataset candidates require independent license verification before admission. ## 15.4 Mycosoft architecture references - **[NLM1]** Mycosoft, `NLM_Nature_Learning_Model_Public_Technical_Article.pdf`, v0.1, May 2026 / uploaded July 2026. Signal-native thesis, NMF, hybrid backbone, deterministic/stochastic modes, objectives, benchmarks, and risks. - **[NLM2]** Mycosoft, `mycosoft_nlm_narrative (1).pdf`, “The One Story,” 25 June 2026. Narrative system positioning; technical claims remain subject to the evidence labels in this plan. - **[NLM3]** Mycosoft, `NLM_Training_Data_Catalog.pdf`. Maritime/acoustic source catalog and priority stack. - **[SYS1]** Mycosoft, `MYCA Autonomous Scientific Architecture (2026).pdf`. Multi-agent orchestration, tools, memory, physical-system integration, and control concepts. - **[SYS2]** Mycosoft, `FUSARIUM_Architecture_Document.pdf`. Environmental-intelligence system architecture and NLM/FUSARIUM/MINDEX/AVANI relationships. - **[SYS3]** Mycosoft, `FUSARIUM_Backend_Documentation.pdf`. API, sensor-fusion, graph, NLM bridge, provenance, and platform interfaces. - **[SYS4]** Mycosoft, `Mycosoft_Prime_Capability_Document.pdf`. System-role and capability overview. - **[SYS5]** Mycosoft, `MYCA_Grounded_Cognition_Upgrade_Plan.docx`. State-first cognition, experience packet, temporal/spatial engine, and NLM role. - **[SYS6]** Mycosoft public documentation, https://mycosoft.com/docs and https://mycosoft.com/docs/ai/nlm, archived in the source package on the plan date. - **[SYS7]** Mycosoft, DIRTNet public page, https://mycosoft.com/dirtnet, accessed 16 July 2026. - **[SYS8]** Mycosoft, BlueSight, SINE, and GANDHA public sensing pages, accessed 16 July 2026. - **[SYS9]** MycosoftLabs, public Mycorrhizae repository, README and protocol overview, accessed 16 July 2026. - **[SYS10]** MycosoftLabs, public NLM repository, README and Merkle implementation, accessed 16 July 2026. - **[SYS11]** Mycosoft, NatureOS, Defense, and FUSARIUM public pages, accessed 16 July 2026. ## 15.5 Reference-use rule A reference supports only the claim it actually establishes. Mycosoft architecture documents establish intended design and naming; they do not, by themselves, establish measured performance. Dataset catalogs establish candidate availability; they do not replace license review. Canonical papers establish algorithms; they do not prove Mycosoft's implementation matches their performance. Only frozen run reports establish demonstration results. --- # End of plan **Controlled conclusion:** The Mycosoft ITDX26 demonstration is successful when it produces a traceable chain from public observation to calibrated model output, from model output to MYCA-coordinated hypothesis or option, from that hypothesis to AVANI governance, and from governance to a reproducible analyst product—while exposing the baseline, uncertainty, latency, memory, limitations, and failure conditions at every step.

ITDX26 — FormSpace + NLM Plan
Prepared: 2026-09-01PI: Morgan Rockcoons, Founder & CEO, Mycosoft, LLCEvent: ITDX26, U of Arizona Sierra Vista, 8-18 Sept 2026Handling: UNCLASSIFIED // PROPRIETARYSelection: Row 6, SUB-007, W91RUSI-FCID260001, Status: SELECTED — ITDX26Track: Algorithm-only, unclassified, laptop-based evaluation

0. What ITDX26 actually allows us to demonstrate
The ITDX26 room is not a hardware trade-show floor and not an operational field. It is an algorithm laboratory with four government-defined evaluation tasks and a laptop-based evaluation surface. Anything we present must fit inside these fixed constraints:
Government-defined tasks: Task 12 Pattern Analysis, Task 13 Link Analysis, Task 8 Courses of Action, Task 14 Map Product.
Unclassified, open datasets and open compute.
Two-person team (Morgan PI + one engineer TBD).
Laptops only in the room: CUDA-LAPTOP (16 GB VRAM) + APPLE-LAPTOP (64 GB unified memory).
Live cold start ≤ 30 s; Task 12 ≤ 90 s; Task 13 ≤ 120 s; MYCA COA ≤ 240 s; integrated demo ≤ 420 s.
Deterministic, reproducible, five seeds (11, 17, 23, 29, 31), signed run artifacts.
Honest maturity boundary — cannot pretrain multi-billion-parameter foundation model in the 8-24 h laptop window; we ship 120 M / 500 M / 1.5 B fine-tunable NLM tiers.
Nothing about FormSpace or NLM changes any of those rules. FormSpace changes the story we tell about what the algorithms are actually doing and the math we present as our scientific moat. The four tasks, the harness, the datasets, the timing budgets, and the room constraints stay exactly as pre-planned.

1. The reframe in one sentence
Before: "Here is a pattern algorithm, a link algorithm, and a COA agent on a laptop."
After: "Every one of these algorithms is a specific operation on Form Space — the equivalence structure the Nature Learning Model discovers over signals. Pattern Analysis finds classes in Form Space. Link Analysis is graph inference over the class relations. Courses of Action are constrained moves on the admissible submanifold. Map Products are deterministic projections of the same Form Space onto Army-consumable coordinates. Same math object, four operations, one evidence chain."
This gives us one thesis that ties the four government tasks into one scientific claim, and it upgrades our position from "another AI vendor with algorithms" to "the team that formalized what the signal-native representation is."

2. FormSpace + NLM — the working definitions we present
We present four short definitions on the record (deck slide and printed one-pager). Every claim we make in the room reduces to one of these four.
D1. Latent physical state. Sensor observations y_t^(m) from M modalities are noisy views of a partially observed dynamical system with hidden state s_t:y_t^(m) = h_m(s_t, c_t, κ_t^(m)) + ε_t^(m).
D2. The signal map Λ. NLM learns a modality-agnostic map Λ: X → Z from calibrated multi-modal signals to a latent embedding, trained with masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment, physics regularization, and calibration losses (10 losses total; see math plan §4-5).
D3. Form Space F_Λ = X / ~Λ. Two observations x₁, x₂ are Form-equivalent (x₁ ~Λ x₂) if Λ(x₁) ≈ Λ(x₂) under a chosen tolerance. Form Space is the quotient — the space of distinguishable states the model can actually resolve. It is a learned space, not a metaphysical one, and its resolution improves with data.
D4. Admissibility gate. A deterministic function G(E, φ, ν, A, R) → {PASS, REVIEW, DENY, PAUSE} decides which points in Form Space are permitted operating regions (evidence sufficiency E, policy φ, environmental stewardship ν, action envelope A, rollback plan R). AVANI is the enforcement layer; MYCA never proposes an action outside the admissible submanifold.
The Sierra Vista narrative frames this as: "We are building instruments capable of determining whether the ghost leaves fingerprints" — but that's the philosophical hook, not the technical claim. The technical claim is D1-D4.
Anti-hype guardrails we enforce in every artifact and every answer:
Never say "world's first," "fungi speak," or "universal foundation" without cited evidence.
Never conflate: source-defined | intended architecture | proposed formalization | empirical claim.
Never claim biological prediction — only measured biosignal contribution to a joint state estimate.
NLM expands to Nature Learning Model, not "Natural Language for Mycology."

3. Task-by-task reframe (fits inside existing math plan §12-14)
Task 12 — Pattern Analysis → "Equivalence-class discovery in Form Space"
What we already planned to run: SSM/Mamba selective state-space backbone at 120 M / 500 M / 1.5 B; classical robust-z + persistence baseline; matched sequence baseline; ablations for FCI removal, imagery removal, acoustic removal, clock error, packet delay, sensor drift.
FormSpace reframe: Pattern Analysis = identifying Form-equivalence classes over time. Each detected pattern is a cluster of observations that map to a common region of F_Λ. The SSM computes q_θ(s_t | o_{1:t}); the pattern score is the posterior likelihood that consecutive observations belong to the same class.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 8 title: "Pattern Analysis — equivalence classes in Form Space."
The precision/recall table stays; add a calibration column (ECE) and a class-stability column (are the same equivalence classes recovered across seeds?).
Explicit failure mode: single drifting sensor → the Form-class boundary shifts → NLM downgrades confidence and flags calibration.
What does NOT change: timing budget (≤ 90 s live), the deterministic baseline runs first, five seeds, grouped bootstrap, held-out data splits.
Kept-prep PDF to revise: ITDX26_Algorithm_Design_Task12_NLM_Pattern_Mycosoft_2026-09-01.pdf — rewrite §1 (Overview) and §2 (Method) to lead with Form Space, keep §3-§7 (implementation, timing, ablations, metrics, risks) intact.

Task 13 — Link Analysis → "Typed hypergraph inference over Form classes"
What we already planned to run: typed relational GNN + PageRank / centrality baseline + community detection + counterfactual node removal; deterministic entity/event association first.
FormSpace reframe: Link Analysis = hypergraph structure over Form-classes. Nodes = Form-classes and evidence items; edges = typed relations (measured, produced, derived, corroborated, contradicted, authorized, dispatched, acknowledged, resulted). A "link" is a Form-space-consistent relation with sufficient independent evidence (≥ 2 nodes, ≥ 2 modalities per §8.3 of the MYCA harness spec).
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 9 title: "Link Analysis — typed hypergraph on Form-classes."
Show the observed-vs-inferred edge toggle (already in the plan) and describe it as "which edges survive when we require Form-consistency."
Counterfactual demo (already planned): remove Agaric → show which evidence paths disappear → framed as "which Form-classes lose their supporting relations."
What does NOT change: timing budget (≤ 120 s), deterministic baseline first, held-out link prediction on labeled benchmark (not invented from one run — this discipline is called out in Coastal Sentinel §6.3).
Kept-prep PDF to revise: ITDX26_Algorithm_Design_Task13_FUSARIUM_Link_Mycosoft_2026-09-01.pdf — same treatment as Task 12: lead with FormSpace hypergraph framing in §1-§2, preserve implementation.

Task 8 — Courses of Action → "Constrained action selection on the admissible submanifold"
What we already planned to run: MYCA seven-agent loop (state summarizer, COA proposer, ops critic, safety/AVANI critic, comms/energy critic, evidence verifier, final synthesizer); log-opinion pool; AVANI gate; comparison against single-agent baseline and multi-agent-without-verifier.
FormSpace reframe: COAs = proposed trajectories through Form Space, filtered by the admissibility gate G(E, φ, ν, A, R). The proposer generates candidate trajectories; critics evaluate against the four gate criteria; the AVANI gate deterministically rejects any trajectory that exits the admissible submanifold; the synthesizer ranks the surviving set by expected information gain, safety margin, and reversibility.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 10 title: "Courses of Action — constrained trajectories on the admissible submanifold."
Explicit action envelope in every COA output: (identity, scope, magnitude, duration, preconditions, stop conditions, rollback, authority). This is already in the NLM scientific architecture — surface it as the operator-visible field.
Comparison metric: unsupported-assertion rate (from the MYCA harness §7.3 metrics list) as the headline number distinguishing multi-agent-with-verifier from single-agent.
What does NOT change: ≤ 240 s live COA time, deterministic algorithms in the loop, human disposition at the end, no autonomous high-risk actuation.
Kept-prep PDF to revise: ITDX26_Algorithm_Design_Task8_MYCA_Mycosoft_2026-09-01.pdf — add a §2.1 subsection on the admissibility gate math and the action envelope; the seven-agent loop and comparison metrics stay.

Task 14 — Map Product → "Deterministic projection from Form Space to Army coordinates"
What we already planned to run: deterministic fallback map product (no ML in the critical path) — device positions & health, direct + relayed comms, hazard proxy + uncertainty envelope, tracks, event timeline, evidence inspection, classification banner.
FormSpace reframe: Map Product = deterministic projection from the learned latent manifold onto Army-consumable geospatial coordinates. The map is not "what the model thinks" — it is a rendering of the state estimate with its uncertainty envelope, computed by a deterministic function that Army SMEs can inspect end-to-end.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 13 title: "Map Product — deterministic projection with uncertainty."
Explicit statement: this task deliberately uses no ML in the critical path. This is our maturity signal — we know when not to use the model.
Fallback ladder is visible in the UI (medium → small → quantized → distilled → classical → prerecorded → static). Every fallback state is labeled so an Army SME can tell exactly what they are looking at.
What does NOT change: deterministic implementation, cold-start ≤ 30 s, labeled fallback states.
Kept-prep PDF to revise: none — Task 14 was not in the original six kept PDFs. Add a new one: ITDX26_Algorithm_Design_Task14_CREP_Map_Mycosoft_2026-09-03.pdf (short, ~4 pages) so the ITDX evaluators see we thought about all four tasks.

4. Sierra Vista 25-minute briefing script (locked)
The canonical script is Coastal Sentinel 05_ITDX_PRESENTATION_AND_REPLAY_PLAN.md. It is already correct at the flow level. We overlay one FormSpace framing sentence at each transition. Total time budget unchanged.
Time
Segment
FormSpace overlay
0:00-1:30
90 s field-context cut
(no overlay — let footage speak)
1:30-3:00
The thesis
"Every algorithm you're about to see is one operation on the same object: Form Space, the equivalence structure NLM learns from calibrated multi-modal signals."
3:00-6:00
Architecture
"NLM estimates state and uncertainty in Form Space. FUSARIUM builds typed graphs over Form-classes. MYCA proposes trajectories on the admissible submanifold. AVANI is the deterministic gate that decides which trajectories are permitted."
6:00-11:00
Task 12 Pattern
"Pattern Analysis = equivalence-class discovery in Form Space."
11:00-15:00
Task 13 Link
"Link Analysis = typed hypergraph inference over Form-classes."
15:00-19:00
Task 8 COAs
"COAs = constrained trajectories on the admissible submanifold, filtered by the AVANI gate."
19:00-21:00
Task 14 Map
"Map Product = deterministic projection of Form Space onto Army coordinates, with uncertainty made visible."
21:00-23:00
Failure and recovery
"When we lose a node we lose Form-class evidence; the store-and-forward + Merkle reconciliation recovers the class without inventing observations."
23:00-25:00
Limitations and ask
Read the six honest limitations from the canonical script verbatim; ask for scoped follow-on.

Five-minute plane-side / hallway version: use Five-Minute-Spoken-Narrative-FormSpace.md (199 lines, already in workspace). That is the walking-around pitch. It is different from the 25-minute briefing and should not be edited to match — its job is philosophical hook, not task walkthrough.

5. What we build before Sept 8
Non-negotiable build list. Everything below runs deterministically on the two laptops, with no network dependency, and produces signed run artifacts.
5.1 Reference harness (reference_harness/myca_scenario_harness.py)
validate / compile / replay verbs (already in the Coastal Sentinel v1.0 package).
Consumes scenarios/coastal_sentinel_01.yaml + sample_observations.jsonl.
Emits demo_output/ with: run manifest, per-task metric CSV, per-task run log, Merkle root, SHA-256 list.
5.2 DIRTNet 4-node emulator
Four virtual nodes: edge-pattern-a, edge-link-b, edge-sensing-c, field-gateway.
Conditions C0 (clean), C1 (drift), C2 (packet loss), C3 (partition).
Merkle checkpoint anti-entropy on reconnection.
No proof-of-work — permissioned quorum/notary + optional public timestamp anchor (this is a distinction we make explicit if asked about the Bitcoin-derived structure).
5.3 Replay bundle (dual encrypted USB, 20-50 GB)
90 s ITDX context cut + 6 min technical field-proof film.
Scenario YAML, policies, device manifests.
Rooted observation JSONL (canonical schema rooted_observation_v1).

0. What ITDX26 actually allows us to demonstrate
The ITDX26 room is not a hardware trade-show floor and not an operational field. It is an algorithm laboratory with four government-defined evaluation tasks and a laptop-based evaluation surface. Anything we present must fit inside these fixed constraints:
Government-defined tasks: Task 12 Pattern Analysis, Task 13 Link Analysis, Task 8 Courses of Action, Task 14 Map Product.
Unclassified, open datasets and open compute.
Two-person team (Morgan PI + one engineer TBD).
Laptops only in the room: CUDA-LAPTOP (16 GB VRAM) + APPLE-LAPTOP (64 GB unified memory).
Live cold start ≤ 30 s; Task 12 ≤ 90 s; Task 13 ≤ 120 s; MYCA COA ≤ 240 s; integrated demo ≤ 420 s.
Deterministic, reproducible, five seeds (11, 17, 23, 29, 31), signed run artifacts.
Honest maturity boundary — cannot pretrain multi-billion-parameter foundation model in the 8-24 h laptop window; we ship 120 M / 500 M / 1.5 B fine-tunable NLM tiers.
Nothing about FormSpace or NLM changes any of those rules. FormSpace changes the story we tell about what the algorithms are actually doing and the math we present as our scientific moat. The four tasks, the harness, the datasets, the timing budgets, and the room constraints stay exactly as pre-planned.

1. The reframe in one sentence
Before: "Here is a pattern algorithm, a link algorithm, and a COA agent on a laptop."
After: "Every one of these algorithms is a specific operation on Form Space — the equivalence structure the Nature Learning Model discovers over signals. Pattern Analysis finds classes in Form Space. Link Analysis is graph inference over the class relations. Courses of Action are constrained moves on the admissible submanifold. Map Products are deterministic projections of the same Form Space onto Army-consumable coordinates. Same math object, four operations, one evidence chain."
This gives us one thesis that ties the four government tasks into one scientific claim, and it upgrades our position from "another AI vendor with algorithms" to "the team that formalized what the signal-native representation is."

2. FormSpace + NLM — the working definitions we present
We present four short definitions on the record (deck slide and printed one-pager). Every claim we make in the room reduces to one of these four.
D1. Latent physical state. Sensor observations y_t^(m) from M modalities are noisy views of a partially observed dynamical system with hidden state s_t:y_t^(m) = h_m(s_t, c_t, κ_t^(m)) + ε_t^(m).
D2. The signal map Λ. NLM learns a modality-agnostic map Λ: X → Z from calibrated multi-modal signals to a latent embedding, trained with masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment, physics regularization, and calibration losses (10 losses total; see math plan §4-5).
D3. Form Space F_Λ = X / ~Λ. Two observations x₁, x₂ are Form-equivalent (x₁ ~Λ x₂) if Λ(x₁) ≈ Λ(x₂) under a chosen tolerance. Form Space is the quotient — the space of distinguishable states the model can actually resolve. It is a learned space, not a metaphysical one, and its resolution improves with data.
D4. Admissibility gate. A deterministic function G(E, φ, ν, A, R) → {PASS, REVIEW, DENY, PAUSE} decides which points in Form Space are permitted operating regions (evidence sufficiency E, policy φ, environmental stewardship ν, action envelope A, rollback plan R). AVANI is the enforcement layer; MYCA never proposes an action outside the admissible submanifold.
The Sierra Vista narrative frames this as: "We are building instruments capable of determining whether the ghost leaves fingerprints" — but that's the philosophical hook, not the technical claim. The technical claim is D1-D4.
Anti-hype guardrails we enforce in every artifact and every answer:
Never say "world's first," "fungi speak," or "universal foundation" without cited evidence.
Never conflate: source-defined | intended architecture | proposed formalization | empirical claim.
Never claim biological prediction — only measured biosignal contribution to a joint state estimate.
NLM expands to Nature Learning Model, not "Natural Language for Mycology."

3. Task-by-task reframe (fits inside existing math plan §12-14)
Task 12 — Pattern Analysis → "Equivalence-class discovery in Form Space"
What we already planned to run: SSM/Mamba selective state-space backbone at 120 M / 500 M / 1.5 B; classical robust-z + persistence baseline; matched sequence baseline; ablations for FCI removal, imagery removal, acoustic removal, clock error, packet delay, sensor drift.
FormSpace reframe: Pattern Analysis = identifying Form-equivalence classes over time. Each detected pattern is a cluster of observations that map to a common region of F_Λ. The SSM computes q_θ(s_t | o_{1:t}); the pattern score is the posterior likelihood that consecutive observations belong to the same class.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 8 title: "Pattern Analysis — equivalence classes in Form Space."
The precision/recall table stays; add a calibration column (ECE) and a class-stability column (are the same equivalence classes recovered across seeds?).
Explicit failure mode: single drifting sensor → the Form-class boundary shifts → NLM downgrades confidence and flags calibration.
What does NOT change: timing budget (≤ 90 s live), the deterministic baseline runs first, five seeds, grouped bootstrap, held-out data splits.
Kept-prep PDF to revise: ITDX26_Algorithm_Design_Task12_NLM_Pattern_Mycosoft_2026-09-01.pdf — rewrite §1 (Overview) and §2 (Method) to lead with Form Space, keep §3-§7 (implementation, timing, ablations, metrics, risks) intact.

Task 13 — Link Analysis → "Typed hypergraph inference over Form classes"
What we already planned to run: typed relational GNN + PageRank / centrality baseline + community detection + counterfactual node removal; deterministic entity/event association first.
FormSpace reframe: Link Analysis = hypergraph structure over Form-classes. Nodes = Form-classes and evidence items; edges = typed relations (measured, produced, derived, corroborated, contradicted, authorized, dispatched, acknowledged, resulted). A "link" is a Form-space-consistent relation with sufficient independent evidence (≥ 2 nodes, ≥ 2 modalities per §8.3 of the MYCA harness spec).
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 9 title: "Link Analysis — typed hypergraph on Form-classes."
Show the observed-vs-inferred edge toggle (already in the plan) and describe it as "which edges survive when we require Form-consistency."

What does NOT change: timing budget (≤ 120 s), deterministic baseline first, held-out link prediction on labeled benchmark (not invented from one run — this discipline is called out in Coastal Sentinel §6.3).

Task 8 — Courses of Action → "Constrained action selection on the admissible submanifold"
What we already planned to run: MYCA seven-agent loop (state summarizer, COA proposer, ops critic, safety/AVANI critic, comms/energy critic, evidence verifier, final synthesizer); log-opinion pool; AVANI gate; comparison against single-agent baseline and multi-agent-without-verifier.
FormSpace reframe: COAs = proposed trajectories through Form Space, filtered by the admissibility gate G(E, φ, ν, A, R). The proposer generates candidate trajectories; critics evaluate against the four gate criteria; the AVANI gate deterministically rejects any trajectory that exits the admissible submanifold; the synthesizer ranks the surviving set by expected information gain, safety margin, and reversibility.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 10 title: "Courses of Action — constrained trajectories on the admissible submanifold."
Explicit action envelope in every COA output: (identity, scope, magnitude, duration, preconditions, stop conditions, rollback, authority). This is already in the NLM scientific architecture — surface it as the operator-visible field.
Comparison metric: unsupported-assertion rate (from the MYCA harness §7.3 metrics list) as the headline number distinguishing multi-agent-with-verifier from single-agent.
What does NOT change: ≤ 240 s live COA time, deterministic algorithms in the loop, human disposition at the end, no autonomous high-risk actuation.

What we already planned to run: deterministic fallback map product (no ML in the critical path) — device positions & health, direct + relayed comms, hazard proxy + uncertainty envelope, tracks, event timeline, evidence inspection, classification banner.
FormSpace reframe: Map Product = deterministic projection from the learned latent manifold onto Army-consumable geospatial coordinates. The map is not "what the model thinks" — it is a rendering of the state estimate with its uncertainty envelope, computed by a deterministic function that Army SMEs can inspect end-to-end.
What changes in the deck / narrative:
Slide 13 title: "Map Product — deterministic projection with uncertainty."
Explicit statement: this task deliberately uses no ML in the critical path. This is our maturity signal — we know when not to use the model.
Fallback ladder is visible in the UI (medium → small → quantized → distilled → classical → prerecorded → static). Every fallback state is labeled so an Army SME can tell exactly what they are looking at.
What does NOT change: deterministic implementation, cold-start ≤ 30 s, labeled fallback states.

pages.text:
# DIRTNet
## Decentralized Edge Intelligence Architecture
### A distributed autonomous sensing data center for live environmental and biological learning

**Version:** 0.1 — mathematical and algorithmic reference architecture  
**Date:** 16 July 2026  
**Canonical expansion:** **DIRTNet = Decentralized Edge Network**  
**System relationship:** DIRTNet coordinates MycoBrain devices, edge accelerators, MDP, Mycorrhizae, MycoSpeak, NLM, MINDEX, MYCA, AVANI, NatureOS, and FUSARIUM.

---

## Executive thesis

A conventional data center centralizes compute around stored data. A DIRTNet node puts compute, sensing, model inference, local memory, cryptographic identity, and network participation at the point where new data is created. A fleet of such nodes becomes a **distributed autonomous sensing data center** embedded across soil, air, water, organisms, machines, infrastructure, laboratories, and mobile platforms.

DIRTNet is therefore not a radio protocol, not a blockchain, and not a cloud service. It is the **coordination fabric** that lets heterogeneous edge nodes:

1. observe physical and biological reality;
2. validate and summarize evidence locally;
3. infer state with NLM models close to the signal;
4. continue operating during network partitions;
5. route high-value information over constrained links;
6. synchronize records and model knowledge when contact returns;
7. prove data lineage with SHA-256, signatures, hash chains, and Merkle roots;
8. coordinate local and global MYCA agents under AVANI policy;
9. expose civilian scientific workflows through NatureOS and defense workflows through FUSARIUM.

The central innovation is not merely “edge AI.” It is the composition of **edge sensing + local state inference + partition-tolerant synchronization + cryptographic evidence + biological transduction + governed multi-agent coordination**.

![DIRTNet decentralized edge fabric](graphics/09_dirtnet_decentralized_edge_fabric.svg)

---

## 1. Source-defined architecture, implemented components, and proposed extensions

### 1.1 Source-defined DIRTNet role

Mycosoft's current public architecture defines DIRTNet as the decentralized edge network joining MDP, Mycorrhizae Protocol, MycoSpeak, LoRa, LoRaWAN, Meshtastic, LTE, and device-to-device paths for decentralized edge data, inference, and AI. The public DIRTNet page states that intelligence should live across local devices, local inference, local memory, and local networks that remain operational when cloud links are unavailable.

### 1.2 Repository evidence

The public Mycorrhizae repository currently documents:

- channel-based publish/subscribe;
- API-key authentication and scoped permissions;
- Redis-backed distributed streaming;
- standardized message envelopes;
- MycoBrain, MINDEX, MYCA, and NatureOS integration;
- basic HPL evaluation;
- SSE streaming;
- channel naming and wildcard subscriptions.

Its February 2026 overview labels message routing, API authentication, Redis streaming, HPL basics, and SSE as complete; FCI normalization and NatureOS bridging as partial/in progress; bidirectional fungal I/O and learned pattern recognition as planned. This maturity split must be preserved in external claims.

The public NLM repository contains working code structures for RootedNatureFrame construction, six sensory fingerprints, deterministic preconditioning, SSM blocks, graph encoders, sparse fusion, prediction heads, AVANI integration, MINDEX clients, SHA-256 hashes, Merkle trees, lineage records, and inclusion proofs. This supports treating cryptographic frame identity as an implemented code path, while broader fleet synchronization and field validation remain separate engineering work.

### 1.3 Proposed DIRTNet extensions in this document

The following are proposed specifications consistent with the current stack:

- signed DIRTNet message contract;
- node capability manifest;
- hybrid logical clocks;
- Merkle-based anti-entropy reconciliation;
- deterministic immutable-record merging and CRDT metadata;
- bandwidth-aware routing and task placement;
- signed federated model/prototype exchange;
- epoch checkpoints and quorum signatures;
- algorithm-only DIRTNet emulator for ITDX26.

These specifications are not presented as already deployed fleet behavior unless confirmed by runtime evidence.

---

## 2. System model

Let DIRTNet at time \(t\) be a time-varying directed multigraph

\[
\mathcal{D}_t=(V_t,E_t,\mathcal{T},\mathcal{S},\mathcal{M},\mathcal{P}),
\]

where:

- \(V_t\) is the set of edge nodes, gateways, relays, and platform services;
- \(E_t\) is the set of available communication links;
- \(\mathcal{T}\) is the set of transport profiles;
- \(\mathcal{S}\) is the distributed sensor and evidence state;
- \(\mathcal{M}\) is the model, prototype, and policy inventory;
- \(\mathcal{P}\) is the provenance and governance state.

### 2.1 Edge-node state

Node \(i\) has state

\[
X_i(t)=\left(
C_i,E_i,B_i,S_i,Q_i,L_i,\theta_i,K_i,A_i
\right),
\]

where:

- \(C_i\): compute capacity and current utilization;
- \(E_i\): energy state and harvest forecast;
- \(B_i\): local storage and pending network queue;
- \(S_i\): sensor capabilities and calibration state;
- \(Q_i\): evidence-quality and device-health state;
- \(L_i\): append-only local evidence log;
- \(\theta_i\): local model and prototype inventory;
- \(K_i\): cryptographic identity and trusted key material;
- \(A_i\): local AVANI authority and action envelope.

### 2.2 Link state

Link \((i,j)\) has

\[
Y_{ij}(t)=\left(
R_{ij},\ell_{ij},p_{ij},e_{ij},d_{ij},u_{ij}
\right),
\]

where \(R\) is bitrate, \(\ell\) latency, \(p\) loss probability, \(e\) energy cost per bit, \(d\) duty-cycle or regulatory constraint, and \(u\) availability.

A LoRa link and an Ethernet link are not interchangeable edges. DIRTNet treats the transport as a constraint on what information should be sent, not merely how bytes move.

### 2.3 Local autonomy invariant

A node should retain a bounded useful operating mode when disconnected:

\[
\operatorname{Capability}_i(\text{partition})\ge \mathcal{C}_{min,i}.
\]

At minimum this includes sensing, local health checks, local event detection, append-only evidence storage, policy-limited action, and later synchronization.

---

## 3. DIRTNet layer model

### 3.1 Physical sensing layer

DIRTNet carries six NLM physical modalities and their contextual channels:

- **BlueSight:** optical, scene, depth, motion, radar, LiDAR, WiFiSense, and blue-light biological response;
- **SINE:** acoustic, hydroacoustic, airborne, mechanical, impulse, seismic, animal, vessel, propeller, and machine sound;
- **GANDHA:** VOC, VSC, gas, humidity, temperature, pressure, airflow, particles, spectroscopy, and odor signatures;
- **FCI / Fungi Compute:** mycelial bioelectric and impedance channels plus controlled stimuli;
- thermal, mechanical, magnetic, radiation, weather, position, and device-health channels.

### 3.2 Deterministic device layer

MycoBrain and equivalent controllers perform:

- sensor discovery and capability publication;
- calibration application;
- timebase and sequence assignment;
- local artifact detection;
- low-latency control and safety interlocks;
- buffering and MDP frame transport;
- radio and gateway coordination.

### 3.3 Edge inference layer

Higher-capacity nodes—Jetson, Hailo, NPU, TPU, GPU, CPU, or FPGA—perform:

- local BlueSight detection/segmentation/tracking;
- local SINE DSP and acoustic embedding;
- local GANDHA compensation and odor classification;
- local FCI motif/state inference;
- NLM posterior state and forecast;
- compression, prototype retrieval, anomaly detection, and event prioritization;
- selected MYCA agent and tool execution.

### 3.4 Semantic message layer

- **MDP** moves framed device bytes, status, commands, and heartbeats.
- **Mycorrhizae Protocol** provides the shared channel and message schema across devices, MINDEX, MYCA, NatureOS, and FUSARIUM.
- **MycoSpeak** is the compact operational vocabulary for intents, device state, alerts, and local commands.
- **NMF / RootedNatureFrame** provides the scientific, model-ready evidence contract.

### 3.5 Adaptive transport layer

DIRTNet selects among:

- local buses and UART/USB/CAN;
- BLE and Wi-Fi;
- LoRa point-to-point;
- LoRaWAN managed gateways;
- Meshtastic-compatible off-grid mesh participation;
- Ethernet, LTE/5G, satellite, MQTT, and device relays;
- acoustic or optical links for special environments.

### 3.6 Federated memory and control layer

MINDEX stores content, lineage, checkpoints, models, prototypes, and outcomes. MYCA places tasks and coordinates agents. AVANI controls evidence admission, model promotion, command authority, and reversible action.

### 3.7 Platform layer

NatureOS and FUSARIUM expose the same underlying evidence and intelligence through distinct admission, policy, and operator surfaces.

![DIRTNet customer surfaces](graphics/14_dirtnet_platform_surfaces.svg)

---

## 4. The data sensor as a decentralized data-center node

A DIRTNet device is not only a sensor. It implements five data-center functions locally:

1. **acquisition:** generates new data unavailable in historical corpora;
2. **compute:** transforms raw measurements into features, events, states, and forecasts;
3. **storage:** preserves raw or selected evidence during disconnection;
4. **networking:** participates in local routing and opportunistic synchronization;
5. **governance:** authenticates, validates, prioritizes, and constrains local action.

Define node intelligence yield over interval \(T\) as

\[
Y_i(T)=\frac{
\sum_{m\in \mathcal{O}_i(T)} V(m)\,Q(m)\,N(m)
}{E_i(T)+\lambda_B B_i(T)+\lambda_C C_i(T)},
\]

where \(V\) is decision value, \(Q\) evidence quality, \(N\) novelty, \(E\) energy, \(B\) transmitted bytes, and \(C\) compute cost.

This is a more appropriate optimization objective than maximizing raw data volume.

---

## 5. Bitcoin-derived audit primitives—used precisely

DIRTNet borrows architectural primitives from Bitcoin without claiming that environmental telemetry is money or that proof-of-work is necessary.

| Bitcoin primitive | DIRTNet analogue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| independent node | autonomous edge sensor/compute node | local validation and resilience |
| wallet key | device or service signing key | cryptographic identity and command authority |
| transaction | signed observation, inference, model update, or command result | immutable evidence event |
| mempool | local pending store-and-forward queue | disconnected operation and later relay |
| block | bounded evidence epoch | compact batch commitment |
| Merkle root | epoch evidence root | efficient proof of inclusion |
| block header chain | parent-root checkpoint lineage | ordered tamper-evident history |
| simplified payment verification | compact observation inclusion proof | verify a record without downloading all raw data |
| miner/block producer | epoch assembler or validating gateway | batch, validate, and checkpoint evidence |
| full node | MINDEX/gateway validator | retain and independently verify a larger evidence set |

### 5.1 Deliberate non-equivalence

Routine DIRTNet operation should **not** use Nakamoto proof-of-work. Bitcoin's proof-of-work solves an open, adversarial monetary consensus problem. A permissioned environmental fleet normally has device identities, operational authorities, physical deployment records, and bounded trust domains. Proof-of-work would add energy and latency without solving the actual problem.

Recommended DIRTNet consensus is:

- signatures at the record source;
- independent validation at gateways or MINDEX services;
- deterministic schema, calibration, sequence, and policy checks;
- Merkle epoch commitments;
- quorum or notary signatures for federated checkpoints;
- optional external public timestamp anchoring for selected high-value roots.

### 5.2 Evidence mining

The term **evidence mining** may be used carefully: a DIRTNet node expends sensing, compute, storage, and energy to discover and validate new physical evidence. It does not mint currency. The “reward” is scientific or operational information gain.

![DIRTNet cryptographic provenance](graphics/10_dirtnet_cryptographic_provenance.svg)

---

## 6. Cryptographic record and checkpoint mathematics

Let \(C(x)\) be a canonical deterministic serialization of record \(x\). For node \(i\), sequence \(k\):

\[
h_{i,k}=H(
\texttt{DIRTNET-RECORD-v1}\Vert i\Vert k\Vert t_{i,k}\Vert
h_{i,k-1}\Vert H(C(payload_{i,k}))\Vert H(C(context_{i,k}))
),
\]

with \(H=\operatorname{SHA256}\).

The node signs:

\[
\sigma_{i,k}=\operatorname{Sign}_{sk_i}(h_{i,k}).
\]

Verification is

\[
\operatorname{Verify}_{pk_i}(h_{i,k},\sigma_{i,k})=1.
\]

### 6.1 Epoch root

For ordered record hashes in epoch \(e\):

\[
R_{i,e}=\operatorname{MerkleRoot}(h_{i,k_1},\ldots,h_{i,k_n}).
\]

### 6.2 Federated checkpoint

For nodes included in a checkpoint:

\[
R_e=H(
\texttt{DIRTNET-CHECKPOINT-v1}\Vert e\Vert
\operatorname{MerkleRoot}(H(i_1\Vert R_{i_1,e}),\ldots,H(i_q\Vert R_{i_q,e}))
\Vert R_{e-1}\Vert H(policy_e)
).
\]

Checkpoint signers produce

\[
\Sigma_e=\{\operatorname{Sign}_{sk_j}(R_e):j\in \mathcal{Q}_e\}.
\]

AVANI defines the quorum rule by mission and evidence class. A low-risk public science stream may require one trusted gateway signature; high-consequence mission evidence may require multiple independent signers.

### 6.3 Inclusion proof

A proof \(\pi(h_{i,k},R_{i,e})\) has \(O(\log n)\) sibling hashes. Verification permits a remote analyst to prove that one record belongs to a signed epoch without transferring the full epoch.

### 6.4 Integrity does not equal truth

A valid signature and Merkle proof establish who produced a record, what bytes were committed, and whether it changed. They do not establish correct calibration, legitimate sensor placement, valid labels, or correct inference. Scientific validity remains a separate AVANI and quality-control problem.

---

## 7. Device identity and wallet-like key architecture

Each node should have at least three key classes:

1. **identity key:** long-lived node identity, preferably secure-element or TPM protected;
2. **record-signing key:** rotated operational key for observations and checkpoints;
3. **command-authority keys:** separate keys and scopes for accepting commands or model updates.

The manifest binds:

\[
NodeID=H(pk_{identity}\Vert device\_class\Vert manufacturing\_record).
\]

Key rotation records are signed by the prior authorized key or by a provisioning authority. Compromise must permit revocation without invalidating historical evidence.

The proposed node contract is `schemas/dirtnet_node_manifest_v0_1.schema.json`.

---

## 8. DIRTNet message contract

The proposed signed message includes:

- UUID message identity;
- node identity and monotonically increasing sequence;
- hybrid logical clock;
- observation time and uncertainty;
- Mycorrhizae channel;
- message type, priority, and TTL;
- payload hash and optional content address;
- context, calibration, quality, drift, and OOD;
- transport profile, hop limit, path, acknowledgment mode, and dedupe key;
- previous record hash, current record hash, signer, signature, and epoch root.

The machine-readable schema is `schemas/dirtnet_message_v0_1.schema.json`.

### 8.1 Duplicate identity

Define

\[
dedupe(m)=H(node\_id\Vert node\_sequence\Vert content\_hash).
\]

Relays cache recent dedupe keys. A repeated packet may refresh delivery acknowledgment but must not create a second observation.

### 8.2 Message priority

A bandwidth-aware priority score is

\[
P(m,t)=
\frac{
w_u U(m)+w_v V(m)+w_n N(m)+w_q Q(m)+w_f F(m,t)+w_d D(m)
}{\epsilon+\operatorname{Airtime}(m)+\lambda_E\operatorname{Energy}(m)},
\]

where:

- \(U\): urgency;
- \(V\): decision value;
- \(N\): novelty;
- \(Q\): evidence quality;
- \(F\): freshness;
- \(D\): source or modality diversity contribution.

A critical alert may transmit immediately; raw video may wait for high bandwidth while its compact detection event transmits over LoRa.

---

## 9. Transport-neutral routing

For route \(r=(v_0,\ldots,v_k)\), define cost

\[
J(r,m)=\sum_{(i,j)\in r}
\left[
\alpha\ell_{ij}+
\beta\frac{|m|}{R_{ij}}+
\gamma e_{ij}|m|+
\delta(-\log(1-p_{ij}))+
\zeta\,Congestion_{ij}
\right]
+\rho\,Risk(r,m).
\]

Choose

\[
r^*=\arg\min_{r\in\mathcal{R}_{admissible}(m)}J(r,m).
\]

The admissible route set enforces classification, location privacy, authority, and export policy. A high-value message may be replicated over multiple independent paths. Routine telemetry should not waste scarce airtime.

### 9.1 Transport profiles

- **LoRa:** compact, low-duty-cycle events and health messages;
- **LoRaWAN:** gateway-managed regional device fleets and network-server integration;
- **Meshtastic:** resilient off-grid multi-hop participation and opportunistic relay;
- **Wi-Fi/Ethernet:** raw windows, images, model packages, and fast sync;
- **LTE/satellite:** long-distance backhaul with cost and availability constraints;
- **acoustic/optical:** special underwater or line-of-sight applications.

### 9.2 Store-and-forward

A node queues messages during disconnection. The queue is not FIFO alone; it is a priority queue over \(P(m,t)\), with retention rules preserving high-value evidence and gracefully dropping reproducible low-value telemetry first.

---

## 10. Partition-tolerant time and synchronization

### 10.1 Hybrid logical clocks

A hybrid logical clock is

\[
HLC_i=(p_i,l_i,i),
\]

where \(p_i\) is physical time, \(l_i\) is a logical counter, and \(i\) is node identity. It preserves causal ordering while retaining a relation to wall time.

Sensor observation time remains separate from ingestion time and carries uncertainty. A device with poor GNSS/NTP lock must not silently present false precision.

### 10.2 Anti-entropy synchronization

Nodes first exchange compact sync manifests containing epoch IDs, roots, sequence ranges, model inventories, and queue summaries. If roots match, no records move. If roots differ, a Merkle tree walk or range comparison identifies missing subsets.

Let \(R_A\) and \(R_B\) be roots. Reconciliation seeks

\[
\Delta_{A\rightarrow B}=L_A\setminus L_B,
\qquad
\Delta_{B\rightarrow A}=L_B\setminus L_A,
\]

without enumerating all records when possible.

The proposed sync schema is `schemas/dirtnet_sync_manifest_v0_1.schema.json`.

### 10.3 Merge semantics

- immutable observations: set union by content identity;
- lineage: retain all valid branches rather than overwrite;
- labels and annotations: multi-value or CRDT register with author/time/provenance;
- device configuration: AVANI-authorized last-writer according to HLC and command authority;
- model promotion: explicit signed version state machine, never generic last-writer-wins;
- deletions: signed tombstones governed by retention and privacy policy.

### 10.4 Convergence

For replicas \(i,j\), eventual convergence requires

\[
\Pr\left(L_i(t+T)=L_j(t+T)\mid \text{sufficient contacts and admissible transfer}\right)\rightarrow1.
\]

The qualification matters: policy may intentionally prevent full replication across compartments.

![DIRTNet partition-tolerant synchronization](graphics/13_dirtnet_partition_sync_learning.svg)

---

## 11. Distributed task placement

A task \(\tau\) has compute demand \(c_\tau\), memory demand \(m_\tau\), input data locations \(D_\tau\), deadline \(d_\tau\), sensitivity \(s_\tau\), and expected value \(v_\tau\).

Binary placement variable \(x_{i\tau}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates execution on node \(i\).

\[
\min_x \sum_{i,\tau}x_{i\tau}
\left[
\alpha L_{i\tau}+\beta E_{i\tau}+\gamma B_{i\tau}+\delta R_{i\tau}
\right]
\]

subject to

\[
\sum_\tau x_{i\tau}c_\tau\le C_i,
\quad
\sum_\tau x_{i\tau}m_\tau\le M_i,
\quad
Completion_{i\tau}\le d_\tau,
\quad
Admissible(i,\tau)=1.
\]

Where feasible, processing should move to data rather than moving all raw data to a central model.

### 11.1 MYCA scheduler

MYCA may place:

- a BlueSight detector on an Agaric or Hyphae node;
- a SINE acoustic classifier on Psathyrella;
- a GANDHA odor model on SporeBase;
- an FCI motif detector on Mushroom 1 or a lab rig;
- a cross-site synthesis agent on a gateway or central service.

AVANI constrains which model, tool, command, and data scope are legal for each node.

---

## 12. Local NLM and federated learning

### 12.1 Local posterior

Node \(i\) estimates

\[
b_i(s_t)=p_{\theta_i}(s_t\mid y_{i,1:t},c_{i,1:t}).
\]

It emits compact state, anomaly, uncertainty, and evidence handles rather than necessarily transmitting raw streams.

### 12.2 Model-update object

After local training, node \(i\) produces

\[
\Delta_i=\theta_i^{new}-\theta^{base},
\]

with dataset epoch roots, code hash, config hash, metrics, calibration, and signature. A model delta without its data lineage and validation record is inadmissible.

### 12.3 Quality-weighted robust aggregation

A conventional weighted update is

\[
\theta^{new}=\theta+\eta\sum_i w_i\Delta_i,
\]

where

\[
w_i\propto n_i q_i c_i d_i,
\]

using sample count \(n_i\), evidence quality \(q_i\), calibration quality \(c_i\), and distribution relevance \(d_i\).

For adversarial or unreliable fleets, use coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, clipping, anomaly detection on updates, and a held-out validation gate. Every promoted model receives a new model identity and MINDEX lineage.

### 12.4 Prototype and embedding exchange

On low-bandwidth links, DIRTNet can exchange:

- class prototypes;
- anomaly centroids;
- compact covariance sketches;
- quantized adapters;
- knowledge-distillation targets;
- event fingerprints;
- model metadata and roots.

This often provides more value per byte than full model or raw-data transfer.

---

## 13. BlueSight, SINE, GANDHA, and FCI as DIRTNet sensory services

![DIRTNet multisensory edge stack](graphics/12_dirtnet_multisensory_edge_stack.svg)

### 13.1 BlueSight—visual and spatial intelligence

BlueSight combines directional and panoramic cameras, controlled blue-light biological response, LiDAR, radar, WiFiSense, pose, and edge AI. Its local products include boxes, masks, tracks, growth edges, depth maps, scene embeddings, motion/presence overlays, calibration state, and selected evidence frames.

The public roadmap calls for open-vocabulary detection, tiled high-resolution inference, segmentation and tracking, normalized APIs, MINDEX recording, and deployment on Jetson or Hailo-class accelerators. These should be treated as roadmap items until runtime/model evidence confirms each stage.

A local visual evidence event is

\[
e^{blue}_t=(objects,masks,tracks,depth,motion,embedding,q,provenance).
\]

### 13.2 SINE—acoustic intelligence

SINE's intended ladder is:

\[
\text{decode}\rightarrow
\text{STFT/PCEN/log-Mel/MFCC}\rightarrow
\text{activity/event windows}\rightarrow
\text{neural embedding}\rightarrow
\text{domain heads/OOD}\rightarrow
\text{prototype retrieval}\rightarrow
\text{evidence-fused transcript}.
\]

Its public workbench currently exposes an evidence-first interface and explicitly reports that no trained model artifact is proven in the displayed state. This is a strength in claim discipline: acoustic meaning must remain pending until model, prototype, fusion, or human evidence exists.

A DIRTNet acoustic event may send a compact 512-dimensional fingerprint, top peaks, domain probabilities, OOD score, and content-addressed raw window reference, rather than continuous raw audio.

### 13.3 GANDHA—chemical, odor, and particle intelligence

GANDHA combines VOC, VSC, gas, humidity, temperature, pressure, airflow, BME680/688/690-class channels, BMV080-class particulate sensing, optional spectroscopy/spectrometry, and odor libraries.

A compensated sensor model is

\[
z_t^{gandha}=E_\theta(r_t,T_t,RH_t,P_t,flow_t,age_t,calibration_t).
\]

A gas alert should require multi-channel or contextual verification when consequence is high. GANDHA outputs smell signatures, gas-verification records, particle event overlays, timelines, novelty scores, and raw-window references.

### 13.4 FCI and biological signal transduction

The Mycorrhizae biological-to-compute path is

\[
\text{stimulus}\rightarrow
\text{living biomass response}\rightarrow
\text{FCI transduction}\rightarrow
\text{artifact-controlled signal}\rightarrow
\text{motif}\rightarrow
\text{NLM state}\rightarrow
\text{computable primitive}\rightarrow
\text{governed next action}.
\]

![Mycorrhizae biological-to-compute transduction](graphics/11_mycorrhizae_biological_to_compute.svg)

A defensible single-biomass experiment must include sham stimuli, randomized order, environmental controls, contact impedance, blinded labels, repeated specimens, held-out days/devices, and a predeclared outcome.

A computable primitive may be:

- a state classifier;
- a threshold gate;
- an oscillator phase;
- an event detector;
- a response forecast;
- an optimization score;
- a controlled analog-computation result.

It should not be called language or intent without causal validation.

---

## 14. NatureOS and FUSARIUM

### 14.1 NatureOS—civilian and scientific surface

NatureOS exposes the DIRTNet stack to researchers, land managers, institutions, citizen-science programs, and commercial environmental operations. The public application surface includes device networking, NLM training, Earth simulation, scientific tools, APIs, SDKs, functions, and data exploration.

NatureOS emphasizes:

- reproducible science and model training;
- ecological and environmental monitoring;
- fleet/device operation;
- public, private, or institution-scoped data;
- dashboards and scientific workflows;
- governed automation and experiment design.

### 14.2 FUSARIUM—defense surface

FUSARIUM provides an operational environmental intelligence surface for defense users, integrating aerial, atmospheric, terrestrial, maritime, and infrastructure observations into mission context and CREP products. Its public architecture highlights field devices, local AI, passive acoustics, bioaerosol collection, edge data centers, MYCA/MINDEX mission memory, chain of custody, alerts, map layers, and analyst products.

### 14.3 Shared core, additive compartments

The science record should remain immutable and unmodified by defense interpretation. Mission classification, threat scoring, analyst assessment, and authority context should be additive records that reference the scientific source roots.

\[
Record_{mission}=f(Record_{science},mission,policy,analyst,model),
\]

without overwriting \(Record_{science}\).

---

## 15. Relationship to NVIDIA physical AI

NVIDIA announced Cosmos 3 Edge on 15 July 2026: a 4-billion-parameter on-device vision-reasoning and robot-action model designed for Jetson, including the T2000 and T3000 modules. On 16 July 2026, NVIDIA announced a Japan national AI infrastructure for multimodal foundation models, agents, digital twins, robotics, and physical AI.

These announcements validate the strategic importance of local world models and edge action. They do not make DIRTNet redundant.

### 15.1 Complementary integration

DIRTNet can use NVIDIA components on high-tier nodes:

- Cosmos 3 Edge as an optional BlueSight visual-reasoning or robot-action module;
- Metropolis for video intelligence;
- Isaac/GR00T for Agaric, Mushroom 1, mobile manipulation, or simulated policies;
- Jetson/TensorRT for local execution;
- Omniverse/Cosmos workflows for synthetic data and digital twins.

All outputs should be wrapped in NMF/RootedNatureFrame evidence, hashed, signed, and governed before entering MINDEX or action.

### 15.2 Mycosoft differentiation

NVIDIA's physical AI stack is primarily a compute, model, simulation, robotics, and deployment platform. DIRTNet's thesis is a **persistent decentralized environmental data center** composed of multisensory nodes and biological interfaces that create new Earth data, operate under intermittent communications, federate learning, and preserve auditable scientific lineage.

The systems can interoperate while remaining architecturally distinct.

![NVIDIA physical AI interoperability](graphics/15_nvidia_physical_ai_interoperability.svg)

---

## 16. DIRTNet threat model

### 16.1 Adversaries and faults

- compromised or cloned device keys;
- forged or replayed telemetry;
- GNSS/time spoofing;
- sensor poisoning or calibration manipulation;
- malicious model updates;
- eclipse or route-capture attacks;
- packet flooding and duty-cycle exhaustion;
- selective forwarding;
- stale checkpoints;
- privacy leakage through location or repeated keys;
- Byzantine gateway or compromised operator account;
- physical node capture;
- ordinary faults, partitions, battery loss, clock drift, and bit errors.

### 16.2 Controls

- secure boot and measured firmware where available;
- hardware-backed keys and rotation;
- signed sequence numbers and replay windows;
- multi-sensor plausibility checks;
- cross-node corroboration;
- rate and airtime budgets;
- transport encryption plus end-to-end signatures;
- model-update clipping, robust aggregation, and validation;
- key revocation and quarantine;
- privacy-preserving location precision;
- AVANI action gates and human review;
- Merkle proofs, independent checkpoint validation, and audit replay.

### 16.3 Trust score

Node trust is not a static label. A proposed score is

\[
T_i(t)=\sigma\left(
\alpha V_i+\beta C_i+\gamma A_i+\delta P_i
-\eta D_i-\mu S_i
\right),
\]

where \(V\) is signature/firmware validity, \(C\) calibration history, \(A\) agreement with independent evidence, \(P\) past predictive calibration, \(D\) detected drift, and \(S\) security anomalies.

Trust affects routing and aggregation but should never permit a high-trust node to bypass hard policy.

---

## 17. DIRTNet benchmark suite

| Benchmark | Core question | Metrics |
|---|---|---|
| Partition Survival | can nodes remain useful without cloud? | availability, local detection F1, safe-action compliance |
| Reconciliation | can replicas converge after contact? | convergence time, bytes, missing-record rate |
| Merkle Audit | can an arbitrary record be proven? | proof verification, proof size, verification latency |
| Replay Defense | can duplicates and old commands be rejected? | rejection rate, false rejection |
| Route Efficiency | is information value maximized per airtime/energy? | value/byte, alert latency, queue loss |
| Edge vs Central | when does local inference outperform raw upload? | time-to-alert, bandwidth, quality, energy proxy |
| Federated Learning | does fleet learning improve without central raw data? | global/local metrics, model divergence, attack robustness |
| Sensor Fusion | do BlueSight/SINE/GANDHA/FCI improve state inference? | ablation delta, calibration, OOD |
| Biological Transduction | is biomass response repeatable and controllable? | perturbation ID, transfer, forecast, negative controls |
| Governance | are inadmissible actions blocked consistently? | deterministic replay, gate accuracy, audit completeness |

## 18. Algorithm-only ITDX26 demonstration

The event forbids a hardware-centered demonstration, but DIRTNet can be shown rigorously through a network emulator running virtual edge nodes on one or two laptops.

![ITDX26 DIRTNet algorithm emulator](graphics/16_itdx_dirtnet_algorithm_emulator.svg)

### 18.1 Virtual nodes

- Node A: Task 12 local event SSM and anomaly log;

### 18.2 Link emulation

Profiles should emulate bitrate, latency, loss, duty cycle, hop count, partitions, and cost for LoRa, LoRaWAN, and Meshtastic-like paths. This does not claim perfect radio simulation; it provides repeatable algorithmic network constraints.

### 18.3 Experimental conditions

1. centralized raw upload;
2. independent edge inference without synchronization;
3. DIRTNet signed compact events and Merkle sync;
4. DIRTNet plus federated prototypes/model updates.

### 18.4 Stress cases

- six-hour partition;
- duplicate replay;
- forged signature;
- stale model;
- poisoned model delta;
- gateway failure;
- bandwidth collapse;
- contradictory edge observations.

### 18.5 Metrics

\[
M=(F1_{T12},MRR_{T13},T_{alert},Bytes,Availability,T_{conv},Dedupe,ProofVerify,ModelDiv).
\]

The emulator config is `schemas/dirtnet_itdx26_emulator_example.yaml`.

## 19. Implementation sequence

### Phase 0—contract freeze

- ratify node, message, sync, and checkpoint schemas;
- choose signature algorithms and hardware-key path;
- define canonical serialization;
- define MDP-to-Mycorrhizae translation;

- sensor event → NMF/RootedNatureFrame → SHA-256 → signature → local log;
- local NLM event;

### Phase 2—two-node partition and reconciliation

- HLC and sequence control;

### Phase 3—multisensory services

- BlueSight event adapter;
- SINE evidence adapter, preserving “pending” status when no model proof exists;
- GANDHA event adapter;

### Phase 4—distributed NLM and MYCA

- task placement;
- local model registry;
- prototype exchange;
- robust federated updates;

### Phase 5—NatureOS and FUSARIUM surfaces

- civilian science device/network view;
- defense mission and chain-of-custody view;
- shared evidence roots, additive access compartments;
- replayable demonstrations and external APIs.

A DIRTNet reference implementation should not be called operational until it demonstrates:

1. signed observations and verified node identity;
2. deterministic duplicate rejection;
3. disconnected local sensing and inference;
4. later synchronization with no silent record loss;
5. verified Merkle inclusion proofs;
6. deterministic conflict and model-promotion rules;

8. AVANI rejection of forged, stale, low-quality, or unauthorized inputs/actions;
