text:
[Page 1]
How the Nature Learning Model changed with Form Space
Morgan, the decisive point is this:
Form Space does not replace the Nature Learning Model. It changes what the Nature Learning Model is learning.
Before Form Space, the NLM was primarily designed to answer:
What is the current sensor state?
Is anything anomalous?
What happens next?
Which environmental event or class best explains these signals?
How uncertain is the prediction?
With Form Space, the NLM must additionally answer:
What organized form is this system currently expressing?
Which family of equivalent forms does it belong to?
What target manifold or attractor appears to organize its behavior?
How far is it from that target?
Which forms are possible, reachable, viable, and AVANI-admissible?
How does it recover after perturbation?
Does it know when to stop correcting?
Has its target changed?
Can the same form or competency appear in another substrate?
Which intervention would distinguish competing explanations?
The clean architectural statement remains:
NLM learns Form Space. MYCA navigates Form Space. FCI opens a bidirectional port into biological Form Space. MINDEX stores the Form Space Atlas. AVANI defines its admissible region.
The original fungal-computing program already called for FCI probes, controlled stimuli, signal processing, pattern recognition, machine learning, normalization, and storage in MINDEX. Form Space is the formal world-model architecture that organizes those functions into one coherent scientific system.

1. The honest implementation status
There are three different things in the current materials, and they should not be conflated.
Layer
Status supported by the uploaded materials
First Light NLM
Documented as implemented and live: sensor fusion, 16-dimensional embeddings, anomaly scoring, an HTTP endpoint, self-supervised task definitions, SporeBase labels, and MINDEX persistence.
Sensor-native full NLM
Defined as the intended model architecture: modality encoders, SSM/Mamba temporal processing, graph/hypergraph relations, sparse attention, task decoders, NMF, deterministic and stochastic inference.
NLM Form Space Engine
A proposed architectural and code refactor. The schemas, heads, services, tables, APIs, mathematics, and algorithms are specified, but the uploaded materials do not establish that the complete Form Space stack is already running in production.
That distinction matters. The conceptual architecture has advanced much farther than the verified runtime implementation.
The current working seed is not yet the full SSM/Mamba Form Space Engine. It is a lightweight but legitimate embodiment encoder that created the first grounded sensor-learning loop for MYCA.

2. How the original NLM has been working
2.1 Physical acquisition
The First Light implementation begins with SensorFusionService, which polls MYCA’s embodiment approximately every 100 milliseconds and assembles a NaturePacket.
The packet combines:
BME688 temperature, humidity, pressure, gas resistance, and air-quality information.
FCI fungal electrical measurements.
Jetson camera references or frames.
Audio level and transcription.
Proprioceptive state from attached actuation hardware.
Conceptually:
Pt=(ytenvironment,ytFCI,ytvision,ytaudio,ytbody)P_t= \left( y_t^{environment}, y_t^{FCI}, y_t^{vision}, y_t^{audio}, y_t^{body} \right)
This was the first meaningful correction away from an LLM-first architecture: MYCA acquired an embodied state before language generation.
2.2 The 16-dimensional embedding
The implemented NatureEmbeddingEncoder transforms the current NaturePacket into a normalized 16-dimensional vector:
zt=Eθ(Pt)∈R16z_t=E_{\theta}(P_t)\in\mathbb R^{16}
The documented coordinates include:
Temperature.
Humidity.
Pressure.
Gas resistance.
IAQ.
Fungal signal strength.
Audio level.
Camera presence.
FCI connection status.
Seven derived cross-sensor values.
The endpoint is:
POST /api/nlm/embeddings/nature
Its output is essentially:
{
  "vector": [0.71, 0.65, 0.52, 0.18],
  "anomaly_score": 0.12,
  "ok": true
}
The anomaly score estimates departure from expected sensor ranges:
At=D(zt,Nbaseline)A_t=D\left(z_t,\mathcal N_{\mathrm{baseline}}\right)
where Nbaseline\mathcal N_{\mathrm{baseline}} is the learned or configured region associated with normal observations.
2.3 Initial learning objectives
The initial NLM code defines three self-supervised tasks:
Temporal prediction
P^t+Δ=Fθ(P≤t)\hat P_{t+\Delta} = F_\theta(P_{\le t})
Given the current sensor state, predict a later state.
Contrastive environmental learning
Lcontrast=−log⁡exp⁡(sim⁡(zi,zj)/τ)∑kexp⁡(sim⁡(zi,zk)/τ)\mathcal L_{\mathrm{contrast}} = -\log \frac{ \exp(\operatorname{sim}(z_i,z_j)/\tau) }{ \sum_k \exp(\operatorname{sim}(z_i,z_k)/\tau) }
Packets from the same environment should be represented more similarly than packets from different environments.
Anomaly segmentation
Identify bounded intervals during which multimodal behavior leaves its baseline regime.
SporeBase timestamps add supervised events such as fruiting emergence, contamination, and growth acceleration or deceleration. Those labels align observed biological events with the corresponding sensor windows.
2.4 Initial persistence
The First Light migration created four primary NLM data groups:
nlm_nature_packets
nlm_embeddings
nlm_sporebase_labels
nlm_training_runs
That gave NLM:
Raw observation persistence.
Derived vectors.
Event labels.
Training-run history.
Model-version tracking.
Anomaly-score history.
This is a valid first stage, but it remains closer to an embodiment feature encoder and anomaly service than the complete Nature Learning Model later described.

3. The second NLM: grounded predictive world modeling
The Grounded Cognition plan then expanded NLM from an embedding endpoint into the predictive world-model layer under MYCA.
The important changes were:
Every observation should be wrapped in an audited Experience Packet.
Spatial state should become a first-class model, not optional metadata.
Temporal state should become episodes, event boundaries, and forecasts.
The model should predict future observations conditioned on actions.
Uncertainty should be represented explicitly.
Interventions should be used to learn causal structure.
The LLM should receive grounded structured state only after the NLM and grounding stack operate.
The planned V0 predictive relationship was:
pθ(yt+1:t+H∣y≤t,stspatial,sttemporal,at:t+H,ct)p_\theta \left( y_{t+1:t+H} \mid y_{\le t}, s_t^{spatial}, s_t^{temporal}, a_{t:t+H}, c_t \right)
Its first practical target was simpler:
Given current MycoBrain readings, weather forecast, and time of day, predict the next hour of sensor readings.
This is where NLM stopped being only:
packet → embedding
and became:
history + location + time + action
        ↓
hidden world state
        ↓
future observation distribution

4. The third NLM: sensor-native multimodal architecture
The later technical architecture makes NLM a family of signal-native models rather than one monolithic network.
Examples include:
NLM-Funga
NLM-VOC
NLM-Acoustic
NLM-Spectral
NLM-Soil
NLM-Weather
NLM-Maritime
NLM-MycoNode
NLM-Fusion
The canonical processing chain became:
raw signal
→ calibration
→ artifact filtering
→ feature extraction
→ physical signal token
→ Nature Message Frame
→ modality encoder
→ temporal model
→ graph/hypergraph fusion
→ sparse attention
→ structured state
→ forecast / classification / anomaly
→ language explanation
The architecture is deliberately not transformer-first. Continuous physical streams are long, noisy, unevenly sampled, and often require persistent temporal state. The proposed architecture therefore uses:
Calibration adapters
        ↓
Modality encoders
        ↓
SSM / Mamba temporal backbone
        ↓
Graph / hypergraph interaction layer
        ↓
Sparse cross-modal attention
        ↓
Task decoders
        ↓
NMF / MINDEX
The modality encoders handle different signal physics:
Spectral: RGB, infrared, multispectral and light-field measurements.
Acoustic: waveforms, STFT, Mel, constant-Q, localization and event detection.
Bioelectric: voltage arrays, bursts, electrode geometry, impedance and stimulus-response behavior.
Chemical: VOCs, gases, heater profiles, drift and specimen context.
Thermal: temperature fields and gradients.
Mechanical: pressure, vibration, strain, deformation and seismic data.
Geospatial-temporal: location, elevation, depth, season, weather and recurrence.
A fused latent state is:
ht=Fθ(ht−1,E1(yt(1)),E2(yt(2)),…,EM(yt(M)),ct)h_t= F_\theta \left( h_{t-1}, E_1(y_t^{(1)}), E_2(y_t^{(2)}), \ldots, E_M(y_t^{(M)}), c_t \right)
Hypergraphs were added because environmental events are not naturally pairwise. A fungal response may jointly depend on hydration, temperature, VOCs, substrate, species, prior stimulation and electrode state:
e={vbioelectric,vVOC,vthermal,vsubstrate,vspecies}e= \{ v_{\mathrm{bioelectric}}, v_{\mathrm{VOC}}, v_{\mathrm{thermal}}, v_{\mathrm{substrate}}, v_{\mathrm{species}} \}
That entire relation should be represented by one hyperedge rather than six disconnected pairwise guesses.

5. The fundamental change introduced by Form Space
The previous NLM terminated at a latent state:
zt=Eθ(y≤t)z_t=E_\theta(y_{\le t})
Form Space makes that latent state an intermediate representation.
The revised stack distinguishes four levels:
Symbol
Meaning
xtx_t
Actual physical, biological, robotic, computational, or ecological microstate.
yty_t
What the sensors can measure about that microstate.
ztz_t
Internal multimodal latent representation produced by the NLM encoders.
ftf_t
Typed, chart-local, scientifically interpretable Form State.
btb_t
Posterior over the target, blueprint, setpoint, or attractor organizing the observed trajectory.
Thus:
yt(m)=Hm(xt,e,ct)+ηt(m)y_t^{(m)} = H_m(x_t,e,c_t)+\eta_t^{(m)} zt=Eθ(y≤t(1:M),c≤t,q≤t)z_t = E_\theta \left( y_{\le t}^{(1:M)}, c_{\le t}, q_{\le t} \right) ft=Fθ(zt,Gt,mt,e,ct)f_t = F_\theta \left( z_t,G_t,m_t,e,c_t \right) ft+1∼pθ(ft+1∣ft,at,bt,ct)f_{t+1} \sim p_\theta \left( f_{t+1} \mid f_t,a_t,b_t,c_t \right)
The NLM is no longer learning only an opaque vector. It is learning a structured geometry of organized possibilities.
The Form Space architecture defines this as a typed product:
F=Fmaterial×Fmorphology×Fphysiology×Fbehavior×Fcognition×Fcomputation×Forganization×Fecology\mathfrak F = \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{material}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{morphology}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{physiology}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{behavior}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{cognition}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{computation}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{organization}} \times \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{ecology}}
Not every model uses every component. An acoustic NLM may emphasize physical, behavioral, environmental, and source-identity dimensions. NLM-Funga may emphasize physiological, bioelectric, morphological, ecological, and computational dimensions.
Form Space is explicitly a proposed Mycosoft engineering vocabulary and architecture, not a claim that the software has already proven a literal Platonic realm.

6. Why Form Space must be an atlas, not one vector database
A single universal embedding would imply that the same metric works equally well for:
A fungal colony.
An ocean acoustic field.
A drone fleet.
A weather system.
MYCA’s agent graph.
A laboratory experiment.
A company operating structure.
That is not defensible.
The NLM therefore needs a Form Space Atlas consisting of local charts:
AF={(Ui,ϕi)}i=1N\mathcal A_{\mathfrak F} = \{ (U_i,\phi_i) \}_{i=1}^{N}
where:
UiU_i is a local region of Form Space.
ϕi:Ui→Rdi\phi_i:U_i\rightarrow\mathbb R^{d_i} is the coordinate system for that region.
Transition functions connect overlapping charts.
Examples:
chart:fci:pleurotus:hydration-recovery
chart:fci:pleurotus:nutrient-foraging
chart:maritime:ambient-acoustic-state
chart:psathyrella:vessel-contact-transition
chart:myca:agent-coalition-health
chart:mycosoft:project-delivery-form
This creates several code requirements that did not exist in the original 16-dimensional encoder:
A chart_id.
Chart-selection logic.
Chart-specific metrics.
Chart-version tracking.
Transition maps between charts.
Context and embodiment bindings.
Confidence that the selected chart is appropriate.
Open-set handling when no existing chart fits.

7. How the code contract changes
7.1 Original working code path
sensor_fusion.py
        ↓
NaturePacket
        ↓
nlm/embodiment_encoders.py
        ↓
16-dimensional vector + anomaly score
        ↓
core/routers/nlm_api.py
        ↓
nlm_embeddings
        ↓
MINDEX
Supporting modules included:
nlm/self_supervised.py
nlm/sporebase_labels.py
nlm/bio_tokens.py
nlm/nmf.py
nlm/telemetry_envelopes.py
nlm/translation_layer.py
7.2 Required Form Space code path
Experience Packet / Nature Message Frame
        ↓
calibration + artifact + quality validation
        ↓
modality encoders
        ↓
temporal SSM/Mamba state
        ↓
graph/hypergraph interaction state
        ↓
sparse cross-modal fusion
        ↓
latent world state z_t
        ↓
chart selection
        ↓
Form State inference
        ↓
target / attractor / basin inference
        ↓
transition / reachability / controllability
        ↓
recovery / stop / memory / rewrite
        ↓
FormState object
        ↓
MINDEX Form Space Atlas
        ↓
MYCA Form Navigator
7.3 Correct repository namespace
The corrected top-level namespace should be:
nlm/
  form_space/
    schemas.py
    state.py
    charts.py
    atlas.py
    metric.py
    topology.py
    dynamics.py
    target_manifold.py
    attractors.py
    basins.py
    boundaries.py
    reachability.py
    observability.py
    controllability.py
    recovery.py
    rewrite.py
    invariants.py
    cross_substrate.py
    light_cone.py
    observer_bank.py
    calibration.py
MYCA then receives a separate navigation layer:
mycosoft_mas/
  engines/
    form_navigator/
      goal_contracts.py
      trajectory_planner.py
      collective_form.py
      self_form.py
      rebinding.py
The old proposed namespace blueprint_space/ should not remain the umbrella. Blueprints are target objects inside form_space/.
7.4 New model heads
The original NLM essentially exposed:
embedding
state or class
forecast
anomaly
uncertainty
The Form Space NLM requires:
form_state_head
form_chart_selector
form_metric_head
target_manifold_head
form_posterior_head
attractor_energy_head
basin_membership_head
transition_operator_head
reachability_head
observability_head
controllability_head
recovery_head
completion_stop_head
form_memory_head
form_rewrite_detector
cross_substrate_alignment_head
cognitive_light_cone_head
polycomputation_probe_interface
side_quest_watch_head
uncertainty_calibration_head
These do not all need to be one enormous neural network. Several should be separate estimators or services operating over the shared NLM representation.

8. A practical code refactor
A clean implementation would preserve the existing sensor-native core and place Form Space above it.
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Mapping

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


@dataclass
class FormSpaceOutput:
    latent_state: torch.Tensor
    form_state: torch.Tensor
    chart_logits: torch.Tensor
    target_posterior: torch.Tensor
    attractor_energy: torch.Tensor
    basin_membership: torch.Tensor
    reachability: torch.Tensor
    recovery_prediction: torch.Tensor
    stop_probability: torch.Tensor
    uncertainty: torch.Tensor


class FormSpaceNLM(nn.Module):
    """
    Form Space extension over the sensor-native NLM.

    The base NLM still performs calibrated multimodal encoding and
    temporal/world-state inference. Form Space adds geometry, targets,
    transition structure, recovery, and stopping behavior.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        base_nlm: nn.Module,
        hidden_dim: int,
        form_dim: int,
        chart_count: int,
        target_count: int,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.base_nlm = base_nlm

        self.form_state_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, form_dim)
        self.chart_selector = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, chart_count)
        self.target_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, target_count)

        self.target_prototypes = nn.Parameter(
            torch.randn(target_count, form_dim)
        )

        self.energy_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(form_dim * 2, hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1),
            nn.Softplus(),
        )

        self.basin_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, target_count)
        self.reachability_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, form_dim)
        self.recovery_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, form_dim)
        self.stop_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim + form_dim, 1)
        self.uncertainty_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1)

    def forward(
        self,
        observations: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor],
        context: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor],
    ) -> FormSpaceOutput:
        base = self.base_nlm(observations, context)
        hidden = base.hidden_state

        form_state = self.form_state_head(hidden)
        chart_logits = self.chart_selector(hidden)
        target_logits = self.target_head(hidden)
        target_posterior = torch.softmax(target_logits, dim=-1)

        target_form = target_posterior @ self.target_prototypes

        attractor_energy = self.energy_head(
            torch.cat([form_state, target_form], dim=-1)
        )

        basin_membership = torch.softmax(
            self.basin_head(hidden), dim=-1
        )

        stop_probability = torch.sigmoid(
            self.stop_head(
                torch.cat([hidden, form_state - target_form], dim=-1)
            )
        )

        return FormSpaceOutput(
            latent_state=hidden,
            form_state=form_state,
            chart_logits=chart_logits,
            target_posterior=target_posterior,
            attractor_energy=attractor_energy,
            basin_membership=basin_membership,
            reachability=self.reachability_head(hidden),
            recovery_prediction=self.recovery_head(hidden),
            stop_probability=stop_probability,
            uncertainty=torch.sigmoid(
                self.uncertainty_head(hidden)
            ),
        )
This is still only a model skeleton. A production implementation must add:
Continuous-time support.
Real SSM/Mamba blocks.
Hypergraph context.
Chart-dependent heads and metrics.
Open-set target discovery rather than only fixed target classes.
Explicit action and perturbation history.
Calibrated posterior alternatives.
Missing-modality handling.
Embodiment-conditioned transition operators.
Hard AVANI gates outside the model.

9. Important code cleanup: the NMF naming collision
The source materials currently use NMF in two incompatible ways:
In the First Light file list, nmf.py means non-negative matrix factorization.
In the later NLM architecture, NMF means Nature Message Frame.
That is an avoidable code and documentation collision.
The correction should be:
nlm/matrix_factorization.py
or:
nlm/nnmf_patterns.py
for non-negative matrix factorization.
Reserve:
nlm/nature_message_frame.py
and the acronym NMF exclusively for Nature Message Frame.
Otherwise logs, schemas, imports, API docs, and model-training configurations will become ambiguous.

Previous process

The biggest process change is that passive sensor data alone is no longer sufficient.
To infer a target or blueprint, NLM needs perturb-and-recover episodes:
Establish baseline.
Apply a bounded perturbation.
Observe displacement in Form Space.
Observe whether the system returns.
Measure which region it returns toward.
Test whether it uses more than one recovery route.
Determine whether correction decreases after completion.
Repeat with sham and alternative perturbations.
Compare against a passive relaxation model.
Replicate.

15. How the mathematics changes
15.1 Before Form Space: prediction-centered mathematics
The earlier NLM mathematical objective is principally:
Lbase=λ1Lmask+λ2Lforecast+λ3Lcontrast+λ4Lphysics+λ5Lgraph+λ6Lcalibration\mathcal L_{\mathrm{base}} = \lambda_1\mathcal L_{\mathrm{mask}} + \lambda_2\mathcal L_{\mathrm{forecast}} + \lambda_3\mathcal L_{\mathrm{contrast}} + \lambda_4\mathcal L_{\mathrm{physics}} + \lambda_5\mathcal L_{\mathrm{graph}} + \lambda_6\mathcal L_{\mathrm{calibration}}
It learns:
Reconstruction.
Forecasting.
Cross-modal alignment.
Physical consistency.
Relation prediction.
Calibrated uncertainty.
Those objectives remain necessary.
15.2 Form equivalence
Form Space adds the idea that materially different states may represent the same higher-level form:
fi∼Ifj  ⟺  ∀Ir∈I,∣Ir(fi)−Ir(fj)∣<ϵrf_i\sim_{\mathcal I}f_j \iff \forall I_r\in\mathcal I, \quad |I_r(f_i)-I_r(f_j)|<\epsilon_r
This creates an equivalence class:
[f]I={g∈F:g∼If}[f]_{\mathcal I} = \{ g\in\mathfrak F: g\sim_{\mathcal I}f \}
A blueprint points to this class or manifold, not one exact coordinate.
For example, two fungal colonies need not have identical electrode voltages to occupy an equivalent hydration-recovery form. They must preserve the relevant invariants and recovery dynamics.
15.3 The Form metric
Ordinary Euclidean distance is insufficient. Distance must combine typed domains and causal interactions:
dFS(fi,fj)2=∑kwk(c,e)dk(fi(k),fj(k))2+∑k<lλklΔkl(fi,fj)d_{FS}(f_i,f_j)^2 = \sum_k w_k(c,e) d_k \left( f_i^{(k)}, f_j^{(k)} \right)^2 + \sum_{k<l} \lambda_{kl} \Delta_{kl}(f_i,f_j)
The cross-terms matter. Bioelectric state, humidity and morphology may jointly represent a condition that none of them expresses independently.
The metric should be validated against actual transition and intervention outcomes, not chosen merely because it makes a clean two-dimensional visualization.
15.4 Target manifolds
A target is not one precise state. It is a region:
Mb={f:dFS(f,gb)≤ϵb}\mathcal M_b = \{ f: d_{FS}(f,g_b)\le\epsilon_b \}
This allows acceptable variation.
A healthy target can therefore include multiple morphologies, signal patterns or local implementations that preserve the same function.
15.5 Attractor energy and basins
For candidate target bb, define:
Φb(f,c)≥0\Phi_b(f,c)\ge 0
A stable realization satisfies:
∇fΦb(fb∗,c)=0\nabla_f\Phi_b(f_b^*,c)=0 ∇f2Φb(fb∗,c)≻0\nabla_f^2\Phi_b(f_b^*,c)\succ0
The basin is:
Bb={f0:lim⁡t→∞Tet(f0)=Mb}\mathcal B_b = \left\{ f_0: \lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}T_e^t(f_0) = \mathcal M_b \right\}
The NLM is therefore learning not only where the system is, but the shape of the landscape around it.
15.6 Reachability
A form can be mathematically possible but inaccessible to a particular body.
For initial state f0f_0, embodiment ee, context cc and horizon TT:
RT(f0;e,c)={fT:∃a0:T−1,ft+1=Te(ft,at,ct)}\mathcal R_T(f_0;e,c) = \left\{ f_T: \exists a_{0:T-1}, \quad f_{t+1}=T_e(f_t,a_t,c_t) \right\}
This is one of the most important Form Space corrections.
The system must distinguish:
possible
reachable
viable
AVANI-admissible
Those are not synonyms.
15.7 Recovery
After a perturbation at tpt_p, recovery is:
RRb=1−dFS(fT,Mb)dFS(ftp,Mb)+ϵRR_b = 1- \frac{ d_{FS}(f_T,\mathcal M_b) }{ d_{FS}(f_{t_p},\mathcal M_b)+\epsilon }
A high ratio means the system returned toward the candidate target.
But recovery alone is not sufficient evidence of agency; passive systems can also relax. NLM must compare target-directed models against passive dynamics on held-out interventions.
15.8 Completion and stopping
The system must not merely reach a target. It must recognize stable completion:
Completeb(t)=1Complete_b(t)=1
when:
dFS(ft−j,Mb)<ϵbd_{FS}(f_{t-j},\mathcal M_b)<\epsilon_b
for a sustained interval, and:
E[∥at−jcorrective∥]<τa\mathbb E \left[ \|a_{t-j}^{corrective}\| \right] < \tau_a
Continued growth or action after the target is reached is not successful completion.
This is directly relevant to autonomous agents. An agent that keeps “improving” a completed task can destroy a correct result.
15.9 Form memory and target rewriting
A persistent internal state affects future trajectories:
mt+1=G(mt,ft,at,ct)m_{t+1} = G(m_t,f_t,a_t,c_t)
A target rewrite is supported when a bounded intervention causes the post-washout target posterior to change:
DKL[p(b∣Dpost,washout)∥p(b∣Dbaseline)]>τbD_{KL} \left[ p(b\mid D_{\mathrm{post,washout}}) \parallel p(b\mid D_{\mathrm{baseline}}) \right] > \tau_b
and that new target predicts subsequent recovery behavior better than the original target.
15.10 Cross-substrate form equivalence
Two embodiments can instantiate corresponding forms when a mapping preserves transitions and goal error:
d(ψ(TA(f,a)),TB(ψ(f),ψa(a)))<ϵTd \left( \psi(T_A(f,a)), T_B(\psi(f),\psi_a(a)) \right) < \epsilon_T ∣eAb(f)−eBb(ψ(f))∣<ϵG\left| e_A^b(f) - e_B^b(\psi(f)) \right| < \epsilon_G
This is how the system can test whether a competency discovered in:
Simulation.
A fungal culture.
A different fungal species.
A robot.
A multi-agent architecture.
is genuinely the same higher-level organization rather than a superficial resemblance.

16. The revised training objective
The expanded objective becomes:
LFS=λpredLpred+λmaskLmask+λstateLstate+λmetricLmetric+λattrLattr+λrepairLrepair+λgoalLgoal+λcfLcf+λinvLinv+λxsubLxsub+λreachLreach+λstopLstop+λlightLlight+λcalLcal+λlawLlaw+λMDLLMDL.\begin{aligned} \mathcal L_{FS}={}& \lambda_{\mathrm{pred}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{pred}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{mask}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{mask}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{state}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{state}}\\ &+\lambda_{\mathrm{metric}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{metric}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{attr}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{attr}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{repair}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{repair}}\\ &+\lambda_{\mathrm{goal}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{goal}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{cf}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cf}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{inv}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{inv}}\\ &+\lambda_{\mathrm{xsub}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{xsub}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{reach}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{reach}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{stop}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{stop}}\\ &+\lambda_{\mathrm{light}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{light}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{cal}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cal}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{law}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{law}} +\lambda_{\mathrm{MDL}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{MDL}}. \end{aligned}
The new loss families do the following:
Loss
Purpose
Lmetric\mathcal L_{\mathrm{metric}}
Learn which differences actually matter for transitions, recovery and function.
Lattr\mathcal L_{\mathrm{attr}}
Make states associated with the same stable attractor compact while separating alternatives.
Lrepair\mathcal L_{\mathrm{repair}}
Predict recovery trajectories after perturbation.
Lgoal\mathcal L_{\mathrm{goal}}
Infer target or blueprint posteriors.
Lcf\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cf}}
Predict intervention outcomes, not only correlations.
Linv\mathcal L_{\mathrm{inv}}
Preserve validated invariants across nuisance transformations.
Lxsub\mathcal L_{\mathrm{xsub}}
Align corresponding forms across embodiments.
Lreach\mathcal L_{\mathrm{reach}}
Estimate embodiment-specific reachability.
Lstop\mathcal L_{\mathrm{stop}}
Penalize premature stopping and action after completion.
Llight\mathcal L_{\mathrm{light}}
Estimate a system’s predictive and causal reach.
LMDL\mathcal L_{\mathrm{MDL}}
Prevent inventing a unique “blueprint” for every individual trajectory.
AVANI constraints must remain hard external gates. They should never be reduced to a weighted term that the optimizer can trade away.

17. How MYCA uses the result
The NLM is the cartographer. MYCA is the navigator.
MYCA receives:
Current Form State.
Selected chart and chart uncertainty.
Target posterior.
Nearest attractors.
Distance and direction to candidate targets.
Reachable region.
Viability boundaries.
Candidate trajectories.
Recovery predictions.
Completion and stop probability.
Evidence and provenance.
AVANI disposition.
MYCA then creates a Goal Contract:
{
  "form_space_id": "formspace:mission:v1",
  "target_manifold_ref": "form://target/uuid",
  "desired_invariants": [],
  "acceptable_variants": [],
  "forbidden_regions": [],
  "required_evidence": [],
  "uncertainty_limit": 0.2,
  "resource_budget": {},
  "completion_test": {},
  "stop_conditions": [],
  "rollback_conditions": [],
  "avani_policy_ref": "policy:uuid"
}
MYCA no longer tells every component exactly what low-level step to execute. It specifies:
The target form.
Constraints.
Required evidence.
Resource limits.
Forbidden regions.
Completion conditions.
Repair and rollback authority.
Competent local agents, droids or biological systems solve the detailed path.
That is the software equivalent of communicating a distal morphogenetic setpoint rather than micromanaging every cell.

18. The minimum code migration that should happen now
Migration 1 — Preserve the existing NLM
Do not delete the First Light encoder or endpoint. Reclassify them:
NatureEmbeddingEncoder
→ legacy/simple modality fusion encoder

/api/nlm/embeddings/nature
→ compatibility and diagnostics endpoint
Migration 2 — Resolve NMF naming
Rename non-negative matrix factorization code and reserve NMF for Nature Message Frame.
Migration 3 — Implement the minimum Form State schema
Add:
space_id
chart_id
form_state_id
encoder_state_ref
typed coordinates
target posterior
distance to target
nearest attractors
trajectory velocity
uncertainty
provenance
AVANI status
Migration 4 — Build one atlas, not all of Form Space
The first useful atlas should be narrow:
formspace:fci:pleurotus:v1
with two or three charts:
hydration stability
growth transition
perturbation recovery
Migration 5 — Add offline attractor discovery
Use historical and controlled FCI episodes to discover recurrent terminal regions before putting any Form Space inference in a live control loop.
Migration 6 — Add passive-model comparison
No target or blueprint should be promoted unless it predicts held-out perturbation and recovery data better than a passive model.
Migration 7 — Add trajectory and stop evaluation
Implement:
distance-to-target
recovery ratio
time-to-attractor
overshoot
stop correctness
Migration 8 — Put the Form Navigator behind a feature flag
MYCA may read Form Space outputs in shadow mode before it is allowed to act on them.
The implementation sequence in the canonical architecture is therefore correct:
schemas and terminology
→ offline atlas
→ FCI mapping
→ MYCA navigation
→ PSILO integration
→ cross-substrate transfer
→ visual Form Space Explorer
→ open-ended architecture search

Final interpretation
The Nature Learning Model began as a real, lightweight embodiment-learning system:
NaturePacket → 16-dimensional state → anomaly score
It then evolved into a sensor-native predictive architecture:
calibrated multimodal history
→ temporal world state
→ graph/hypergraph fusion
→ forecast, state and uncertainty
Form Space changes it into a causal and developmental world model:
physical measurements
→ latent state
→ typed Form State
→ chart and metric
→ target manifold
→ attractor and basin
→ reachable trajectories
→ perturbation and recovery
→ completion and stopping
→ atlas update
The most precise one-line description is:
The original NLM learned representations of sensor states; the Form Space NLM learns the geometry, dynamics, targets, memory, reachability and repair behavior of organized systems.
That is a much larger claim, so it also demands much stronger evidence. The right path is not to rename an embedding “Form Space” and declare victory. The right path is to preserve the working sensor pipeline, add charted manifolds and intervention-grounded dynamics incrementally, and require every inferred target or attractor to outperform a passive explanation.

MYCOSOFT Form Space Architecture v2
Architecting Emergent Learning Models

Five-Minute Spoken Narrative
Why I Added Form Space to the Nature Learning Model
Approximate runtime: five minutes at a deliberate speaking pace.

Let me explain how I arrived at this idea.
Imagine that reality is a workshop with two rooms.
In the first room is physics: matter, energy, fields, particles, forces. In the second room is mathematics: prime numbers, geometry, topology, the number ee, and relationships that appear to be true whether or not any particular physical object exists.
Physics can embody those mathematical relationships, but physics does not seem to choose them. Nobody reaches into an experiment and sets ee to approximately 2.718. When a physical process implements continuous growth, decay, rotation, or probability, that mathematical structure is already waiting for it.
That is the sense in which mathematics can be said to haunt physics like a ghost. The ghost does not violate physics. It gives physics some of the patterns it is capable of expressing.
Michael Levin asks a radical but useful question: what if mathematics is not the only structured space haunting the physical world? What if there are also reusable patterns of morphology, behavior, problem-solving, and mind—and physical systems become interfaces through which those patterns appear? He calls that conjectured domain Platonic space. Importantly, Levin presents this as a hypothesis and research program, not as something his experiments have conclusively proven. (Sciety)
The experiment that pushed this question into focus for me was the xenobot.
Xenobots are novel living constructs made from cells taken from Xenopus frogs. The cells themselves are not evolution-free; they inherit billions of years of biological history. But the specific xenobot body, organization, and behavioral repertoire did not previously exist as an evolved animal. Researchers did not insert a detailed genetic program describing a xenobot species. They changed the conditions and organization in which already-competent cells operated, and those cells assembled into motile, coordinated living systems. Later work showed that some configurations could gather loose cells into new multicellular offspring through kinematic self-replication. (PubMed)
Levin states the careful version directly:
“The creatures they make and the capabilities that these creatures have were never directly selected for.”
That does not mean the cells came from nowhere. It means natural selection cannot provide a complete, direct history for that particular organism-level form and every capability it displays. (Lex Fridman)
So where did the organization come from?
The conventional answer is that it emerged from cell mechanics, gene expression, electrical signaling, geometry, and environmental conditions. That answer is not wrong—but the word emergence often means only that the outcome was not obvious to us beforehand. It does not yet give us a predictive engineering theory of which new forms will appear when we construct a particular interface.
Levin puts the problem bluntly:
“Calling them emergent does nothing for a research program.”
That sentence mattered to me. Instead of merely celebrating surprise, we should map the structured space from which these surprises seem to come. (Lex Fridman)
The same issue appears in Levin’s work on sorting algorithms.
His group took familiar, deterministic sorting procedures and distributed the sorting policy among individual array elements. They then introduced defects—such as an element that could no longer move—without adding new instructions telling the algorithm how to respond. In some cases, the system temporarily became less sorted so that it could eventually navigate around the obstruction and complete the task. From a behavioral perspective, that resembles delayed gratification: sacrificing immediate progress to reach a distal goal. (Sage Journals)
They also built chimeric arrays in which some elements followed one sorting algorithm and others followed another. During sorting, elements transiently clustered with others of the same “algotype,” even though the code contained no explicit operation for identifying algotypes or deliberately forming those clusters.
The sorting was the assigned mission. The clustering was an additional behavior. Levin called it:
“It’s a side quest.”
It did not violate the algorithm. A theoretical computer scientist could derive it from the complete dynamics. But nobody explicitly requested it, and it was not visible by simply reading the assigned objective. The architecture made another competency accessible. (Thoughtforms Life Podcast)
That is the bridge to Mycosoft.
Before Form Space, our Nature Learning Model was already philosophically different from a language learning model. A language model begins with symbols produced by humans and predicts relationships among those symbols. It can learn extremely powerful heuristics, but those heuristics are usually downstream of human observation and linguistic compression.
Nature does not begin with words.
Nature begins with voltages, waveforms, chemical concentrations, pressure, heat, light, impedance, movement, growth, damage, recovery, and interaction. Our Nature Learning Model begins there. It asks what physical state generated the observations, what state is likely to come next, and how the trajectory changes under an intervention. Language comes afterward, as an explanation of the grounded state.
But the Nature Learning Model alone could still become a sophisticated pattern detector swimming in an ocean of data.
A forest, fungal colony, coastline, or biological computer produces enormous amounts of variation. Not all variation is meaningful. Some is sensor noise. Some is environmental turbulence. Some is incidental complexity. The needle in the haystack is the persistent organization: what the system remembers, what it protects, where it returns after disruption, and what it can accomplish through more than one path.
That is why we added Form Space.
Form Space is our engineered, testable version of the Platonic-space idea. We do not claim that a nonphysical realm has been proven. We define a measurable space of possible organized states: target manifolds, attractors, basins, barriers, transitions, viable regions, repair paths, and embodied competencies.
The NLM learns the map. MYCA navigates it. MINDEX stores the evidence. The Fungal Computer Interface allows us to observe and reversibly perturb living systems. AVANI constrains which experiments and actions are admissible.
We also use Levin’s cognitive light cone: the region across space and time that a system can measure, model, remember, predict, and influence. Rather than assuming intelligence must speak, we examine the scale of the goals a system can pursue and the perturbations it can overcome. (PubMed)
For a fungal network, that means we do not label every electrical spike a word. We examine whether multimodal signals predict environmental changes, resource allocation, damage, adaptation, or recovery. We apply controlled perturbations, compare the response against passive physical models, replicate the experiment, preserve counterevidence, and reject the blueprint hypothesis when it fails. That is the scientific program behind the FCI and the Global Fungi Symbiosis Theory.
For artificial systems, the same principle means we do not program only one narrow route to one answer. We construct modular interfaces with enough degrees of freedom for unexpected competencies to appear. Then we instrument everything. We identify side quests, test whether they reproduce, determine whether they are useful or dangerous, and never confuse unexpected behavior with proof of consciousness.
So the architecture is not based on blind mysticism. It is based on a disciplined engineering wager:
Perhaps useful forms and competencies exist in a structured possibility space before we know how to explicitly program them.
Our job is to build better pointers into that space—and then test rigorously what comes through.
For the Army, the operational significance is straightforward. A conventional model recognizes what it was trained to recognize. A Form Space system also searches for changing goals, hidden attractors, recovery behavior, collective organization, and capabilities that were not included in the original label set.
The Nature Learning Model improves on language-only intelligence by learning from the physical environment before that environment is translated into words.
Form Space takes the next step. It gives us a way to search the environmental noise for the organizing pattern—the blueprint, if one exists—and to distinguish it from coincidence through prediction, perturbation, recovery, comparison, and falsification.
We are not claiming that we have found the ghost.
We are building instruments capable of determining whether the ghost leaves fingerprints.

pages.text:
MYCOSOFT, LLC
CAGE 9KR60  ·  UEI YK3ARVKJ77S9  ·  451 Acero Place, Chula Vista, CA 91910
FormSpace One-Pager — Mycosoft, LLC — 2026-09-01
Page 1
FormSpace — One-Page Reference
The mathematical object that unifies the four ITDX26 tasks
D1 · Latent physical state
Sensor observations y_t^(m) from M modalities are noisy views of a partially observed dynamical
system with hidden state s_t:
y_t^(m) = h_m(s_t, c_t, κ_t^(m)) + ε_t^(m)
D2 · The signal map Λ
NLM learns a modality-agnostic map Λ: X → Z from calibrated multi-modal signals to a latent
embedding, trained with masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment, physics regularization, and
calibration losses.
D3 · Form Space
Two observations are Form-equivalent when their embeddings agree under the learned tolerance:
x₁ ~Λ x₂ ⟺ Λ(x₁) ≈ Λ(x₂); F_Λ = X / ~Λ
Form Space is the space of physically distinguishable states the model resolves at its current data
budget. Resolution improves with data; the object is learned, not metaphysical.
D4 · Admissibility gate
A deterministic function decides which points in Form Space are permitted operating regions:
G(E, φ, ν, A, R) → {PASS, REVIEW, DENY, PAUSE}
where E is evidence sufficiency, φ is policy, ν is environmental stewardship, A is the action
envelope, and R is the rollback plan. AVANI enforces; MYCA proposes; human dispositions the
result.

FormSpace — One-Page Reference
The mathematical object that unifies the four ITDX26 tasks
D1 · Latent physical state
Sensor observations y_t^(m) from M modalities are noisy views of a partially observed dynamical
system with hidden state s_t:
y_t^(m) = h_m(s_t, c_t, κ_t^(m)) + ε_t^(m)
D2 · The signal map Λ
NLM learns a modality-agnostic map Λ: X → Z from calibrated multi-modal signals to a latent
embedding, trained with masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment, physics regularization, and
calibration losses.
D3 · Form Space
Two observations are Form-equivalent when their embeddings agree under the learned tolerance:
x₁ ~Λ x₂ ⟺ Λ(x₁) ≈ Λ(x₂); F_Λ = X / ~Λ
Form Space is the space of physically distinguishable states the model resolves at its current data
budget. Resolution improves with data; the object is learned, not metaphysical.
D4 · Admissibility gate
A deterministic function decides which points in Form Space are permitted operating regions:
G(E, φ, ν, A, R) → {PASS, REVIEW, DENY, PAUSE}
where E is evidence sufficiency, φ is policy, ν is environmental stewardship, A is the action
envelope, and R is the rollback plan. AVANI enforces; MYCA proposes; human dispositions the
result.

-- STAGED MIGRATION — DO NOT APPLY DIRECTLY TO PRODUCTION
-- MINDEX Form Space Core
-- Rename 00XX to the next free MINDEX migration number before merge.
-- Dependencies: telemetry.device, telemetry.sample, app schema, pgcrypto.

BEGIN;

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS form_space;
COMMENT ON SCHEMA form_space IS
'Canonical Mycosoft Form Space Atlas and scientific lineage.';

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION form_space.touch_updated_at()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SET search_path = pg_catalog, form_space
AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.updated_at := now();
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.model_version (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  model_name text NOT NULL,
  version text NOT NULL,
  model_type text NOT NULL,
  artifact_uri text,
  artifact_sha256 text,
  training_run_ref text,
  evaluation_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  input_schema_version text NOT NULL,
  output_schema_version text NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','validated','shadow','active','retired','rejected')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  activated_at timestamptz,
  retired_at timestamptz,
  UNIQUE (model_name, version)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_model_status
  ON form_space.model_version(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_model_type
  ON form_space.model_version(model_type);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.space (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  domain text NOT NULL,
  definition text NOT NULL,
  ontology_version text NOT NULL,
  coordinate_domains text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  default_metric_id uuid,
  visibility text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'internal'
    CHECK (visibility IN ('public','internal','restricted','classified')),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
    CHECK (status IN ('draft','active','deprecated','retired')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_by text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_space_domain_status
  ON form_space.space(domain, status);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.metric (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  metric_type text NOT NULL,
  definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  context_selector jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  validation_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','validated','active','retired','rejected')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, name)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_metric_space
  ON form_space.metric(space_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_metric_model
  ON form_space.metric(model_version_id);

ALTER TABLE form_space.space
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS fk_fs_space_default_metric;
ALTER TABLE form_space.space
  ADD CONSTRAINT fk_fs_space_default_metric
  FOREIGN KEY (default_metric_id)
  REFERENCES form_space.metric(id)
  ON DELETE SET NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.chart (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  chart_version text NOT NULL,
  dimensions integer NOT NULL CHECK (dimensions > 0),
  coordinate_schema jsonb NOT NULL,
  selector_definition jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  metric_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.metric(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  open_set_threshold double precision
    CHECK (open_set_threshold IS NULL OR open_set_threshold BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','validated','active','retired','rejected')),
  valid_from timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  valid_until timestamptz,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, name, chart_version),
  CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > valid_from)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_space_status
  ON form_space.chart(space_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_metric
  ON form_space.chart(metric_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_model
  ON form_space.chart(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.chart_transition (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  source_chart_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target_chart_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  transform_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  inverse_definition jsonb,
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  validation_error double precision
    CHECK (validation_error IS NULL OR validation_error >= 0),
  validity_region jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN ('candidate','validated','active','retired','rejected')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (source_chart_id, target_chart_id),
  CHECK (source_chart_id <> target_chart_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_transition_source
  ON form_space.chart_transition(source_chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_transition_target
  ON form_space.chart_transition(target_chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_chart_transition_model
  ON form_space.chart_transition(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.embodiment_binding (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  device_id uuid REFERENCES telemetry.device(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  embodiment_type text NOT NULL,
  architecture_hash text,
  capabilities jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  boundary_conditions jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  context jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  valid_from timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  valid_until timestamptz,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
    CHECK (status IN ('active','inactive','superseded','retired')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > valid_from)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_embodiment_system
  ON form_space.embodiment_binding(system_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_embodiment_device
  ON form_space.embodiment_binding(device_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.target (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  name text NOT NULL,
  target_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (target_type IN
      ('manifold','setpoint','blueprint','goal_region','maintenance_region','unknown')),
  manifold_definition jsonb NOT NULL,
  acceptance_metric_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.metric(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  acceptance_epsilon double precision
    CHECK (acceptance_epsilon IS NULL OR acceptance_epsilon >= 0),
  invariants jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  stop_condition jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  context_limits jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN
      ('candidate','supported','cross_substrate_supported','falsified','retired')),
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  evidence_root text,
  falsifiers jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, name)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_target_space_status
  ON form_space.target(space_id, epistemic_status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_target_chart
  ON form_space.target(chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_target_metric
  ON form_space.target(acceptance_metric_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_target_model
  ON form_space.target(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.attractor (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  name text NOT NULL,
  attractor_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (attractor_type IN
      ('fixed_point','limit_cycle','manifold','metastable','switching','unknown')),
  representation jsonb NOT NULL,
  energy_model_ref text,
  stability_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  basin_estimate jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  model_version_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  evidence_root text,
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN ('candidate','supported','falsified','retired')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (space_id, name)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_attractor_space_status
  ON form_space.attractor(space_id, epistemic_status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_attractor_chart
  ON form_space.attractor(chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_attractor_target
  ON form_space.attractor(target_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_attractor_model
  ON form_space.attractor(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.state (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  schema_version text NOT NULL,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  embodiment_binding_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.embodiment_binding(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  observed_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  valid_until timestamptz,
  coordinates jsonb NOT NULL,
  form_signature_ref jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  target_posterior jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  nearest_attractors jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  distance_to_target jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  form_velocity jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  reachable_region_ref text,
  viability_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'
    CHECK (viability_status IN ('inside','near_boundary','outside','unknown')),
  completion_probability double precision
    CHECK (completion_probability IS NULL OR completion_probability BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  stop_probability double precision
    CHECK (stop_probability IS NULL OR stop_probability BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  uncertainty jsonb NOT NULL,
  evidence_root text,
  model_version_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  epistemic_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (epistemic_status IN
      ('observation','candidate','supported','falsified','superseded')),
  supersedes_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  correction_reason text,
  correlation_id uuid,
  causation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  provenance jsonb NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until > observed_at),
  CHECK (supersedes_state_id IS NULL OR supersedes_state_id <> id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_system_time
  ON form_space.state(system_id, observed_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_space_time
  ON form_space.state(space_id, observed_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_chart_time
  ON form_space.state(chart_id, observed_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_model
  ON form_space.state(model_version_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_embodiment
  ON form_space.state(embodiment_binding_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_supersedes
  ON form_space.state(supersedes_state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_observed_brin
  ON form_space.state USING BRIN(observed_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.state_evidence (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  state_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sample_id uuid REFERENCES telemetry.sample(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  evidence_uri text,
  evidence_type text NOT NULL,
  role text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'supporting'
    CHECK (role IN
      ('primary','supporting','context','counterevidence','calibration','control')),
  content_hash text,
  verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (sample_id IS NOT NULL OR evidence_uri IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_fs_state_evidence_sample
  ON form_space.state_evidence(state_id, sample_id)
  WHERE sample_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_fs_state_evidence_uri
  ON form_space.state_evidence(state_id, evidence_uri)
  WHERE evidence_uri IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_evidence_state
  ON form_space.state_evidence(state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_evidence_sample
  ON form_space.state_evidence(sample_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_state_evidence_hash
  ON form_space.state_evidence(content_hash);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.goal_contract (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  schema_version text NOT NULL,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  requested_by text NOT NULL,
  title text NOT NULL,
  target_manifold jsonb NOT NULL,
  acceptable_variants jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  required_invariants jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  forbidden_regions jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  resource_budget jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  evidence_requirements jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  uncertainty_limit double precision
    CHECK (uncertainty_limit IS NULL OR uncertainty_limit BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
  completion_test jsonb NOT NULL,
  stop_conditions jsonb NOT NULL,
  rollback_conditions jsonb NOT NULL,
  repair_authority jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  avani_policy_ref text NOT NULL,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('draft','submitted','planning','gated','approved','active','paused',
       'completed','failed','rolled_back','cancelled','vetoed')),
  correlation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_system_status
  ON form_space.goal_contract(system_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_space
  ON form_space.goal_contract(space_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_chart
  ON form_space.goal_contract(chart_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_target
  ON form_space.goal_contract(target_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.goal_contract_event (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  goal_contract_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.goal_contract(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  event_type text NOT NULL,
  from_status text,
  to_status text,
  actor text NOT NULL,
  occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  payload jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  correlation_id uuid,
  causation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  provenance_hash text
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_goal_event_goal_time
  ON form_space.goal_contract_event(goal_contract_id, occurred_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.trajectory (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  goal_contract_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.goal_contract(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  start_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  terminal_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  trajectory_type text NOT NULL
    CHECK (trajectory_type IN
      ('observed','predicted','counterfactual','planned','recovery','simulation')),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'candidate'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('candidate','selected','active','completed','failed','aborted','rejected')),
  planned_actions jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  predicted_outcomes jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  metrics jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  model_version_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  started_at timestamptz,
  ended_at timestamptz,
  correlation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  provenance jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (ended_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= started_at)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_system_time
  ON form_space.trajectory(system_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_goal
  ON form_space.trajectory(goal_contract_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_start
  ON form_space.trajectory(start_state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_terminal
  ON form_space.trajectory(terminal_state_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_model
  ON form_space.trajectory(model_version_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.trajectory_state (
  trajectory_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.trajectory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sequence_no integer NOT NULL CHECK (sequence_no >= 0),
  state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  predicted_state jsonb,
  expected_at timestamptz,
  observed_at timestamptz,
  role text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'intermediate'
    CHECK (role IN ('start','intermediate','target','terminal','counterfactual')),
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  PRIMARY KEY (trajectory_id, sequence_no),
  CHECK (state_id IS NOT NULL OR predicted_state IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_state_state
  ON form_space.trajectory_state(state_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.intervention (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  goal_contract_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.goal_contract(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  trajectory_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.trajectory(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  intervention_type text NOT NULL,
  parameters jsonb NOT NULL,
  requested_by text NOT NULL,
  requested_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  approved_by text,
  approved_at timestamptz,
  executed_by text,
  executed_at timestamptz,
  completed_at timestamptz,
  reversibility text NOT NULL
    CHECK (reversibility IN ('full','partial','none','unknown')),
  rollback_definition jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  risk_summary jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  avani_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_EVALUATED'
    CHECK (avani_status IN ('NOT_EVALUATED','PASS','GATE','VETO')),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'proposed'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('proposed','gated','approved','executing','completed','failed',
       'aborted','rolled_back','vetoed')),
  result jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  correlation_id uuid,
  causation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  provenance jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_intervention_system_time
  ON form_space.intervention(system_id, requested_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_intervention_goal
  ON form_space.intervention(goal_contract_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_intervention_trajectory
  ON form_space.intervention(trajectory_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_intervention_status
  ON form_space.intervention(status);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.recovery_trial (

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.event_outbox (

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW app.v_form_state_latest AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.system_id, s.space_id)
  s.id,
  s.uri,
  s.schema_version,
  s.system_id,
  sp.uri AS space_uri,
  c.uri AS chart_uri,
  s.observed_at,
  s.valid_until,
  s.coordinates,
  s.form_signature_ref,
  s.target_posterior,
  s.nearest_attractors,
  s.distance_to_target,
  s.form_velocity,
  s.reachable_region_ref,
  s.viability_status,
  s.completion_probability,
  s.stop_probability,
  s.uncertainty,
  s.evidence_root,
  mv.model_name,
  mv.version AS model_version,
  s.avani_status,
  s.epistemic_status,
  s.provenance
FROM form_space.state s
JOIN form_space.space sp ON sp.id = s.space_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.chart c ON c.id = s.chart_id
JOIN form_space.model_version mv ON mv.id = s.model_version_id
ORDER BY s.system_id, s.space_id, s.observed_at DESC, s.created_at DESC;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW app.v_form_goal_status AS
SELECT
  g.id,
  g.uri,
  g.system_id,
  sp.uri AS space_uri,
  c.uri AS chart_uri,
  t.uri AS target_uri,
  g.title,
  g.status,
  g.avani_status,
  g.uncertainty_limit,
  g.created_at,
  g.updated_at
FROM form_space.goal_contract g
JOIN form_space.space sp ON sp.id = g.space_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.chart c ON c.id = g.chart_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.target t ON t.id = g.target_id;

DO $$
DECLARE
  rec record;
BEGIN
  FOR rec IN
    SELECT unnest(ARRAY[
      'space','metric','chart','chart_transition','embodiment_binding',
      'target','attractor','goal_contract','trajectory','intervention','recovery_trial'
    ]) AS table_name
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_fs_%I_touch ON form_space.%I',
                   rec.table_name, rec.table_name);
    EXECUTE format(
      'CREATE TRIGGER trg_fs_%I_touch BEFORE UPDATE ON form_space.%I '
      'FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION form_space.touch_updated_at()',
      rec.table_name, rec.table_name
    );
  END LOOP;
END;
$$;

COMMIT;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.trajectory (

  started_at timestamptz,
  ended_at timestamptz,
  correlation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  provenance jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (ended_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= started_at)

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_system_time

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_goal

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.trajectory_state (

    REFERENCES form_space.trajectory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    CHECK (role IN ('start','intermediate','target','terminal','counterfactual')),

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_trajectory_state_state

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.intervention (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

  rollback_definition jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.recovery_trial (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  uri text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  system_id text NOT NULL,
  space_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES form_space.space(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chart_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.chart(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  target_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.target(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  intervention_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.intervention(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  baseline_state_id uuid NOT NULL
    REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  perturbed_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  terminal_state_id uuid REFERENCES form_space.state(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

    REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

    REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

  route_signature jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,

  model_version_id uuid
    REFERENCES form_space.model_version(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_uncertainty_state

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS form_space.event_outbox (

  event_type text NOT NULL,
  aggregate_type text NOT NULL,
  aggregate_id uuid NOT NULL,
  schema_version text NOT NULL,
  producer text NOT NULL,
  system_id text,
  space_uri text,
  chart_uri text,
  form_state_uri text,
  correlation_id uuid,
  causation_id uuid,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  payload jsonb NOT NULL,
  evidence_refs jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,

  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (status IN
      ('pending','publishing','published','failed','dead_letter')),
  attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempts >= 0),
  available_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  locked_at timestamptz,
  locked_by text,
  published_at timestamptz,
  last_error text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

  ON form_space.event_outbox(status, available_at, created_at)
  WHERE status IN ('pending','failed');
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_outbox_aggregate
  ON form_space.event_outbox(aggregate_type, aggregate_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fs_outbox_correlation
  ON form_space.event_outbox(correlation_id);

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW app.v_form_state_latest AS
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.system_id, s.space_id)
  s.id,
  s.uri,
  s.schema_version,
  s.system_id,
  sp.uri AS space_uri,
  c.uri AS chart_uri,
  s.observed_at,
  s.valid_until,
  s.coordinates,
  s.form_signature_ref,
  s.target_posterior,
  s.nearest_attractors,
  s.distance_to_target,
  s.form_velocity,
  s.reachable_region_ref,
  s.viability_status,
  s.completion_probability,
  s.stop_probability,
  s.uncertainty,
  s.evidence_root,
  mv.model_name,
  mv.version AS model_version,
  s.avani_status,
  s.epistemic_status,
  s.provenance
FROM form_space.state s
JOIN form_space.space sp ON sp.id = s.space_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.chart c ON c.id = s.chart_id
JOIN form_space.model_version mv ON mv.id = s.model_version_id
ORDER BY s.system_id, s.space_id, s.observed_at DESC, s.created_at DESC;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW app.v_form_goal_status AS
SELECT
  g.id,
  g.uri,
  g.system_id,
  sp.uri AS space_uri,
  c.uri AS chart_uri,
  t.uri AS target_uri,
  g.title,
  g.status,
  g.avani_status,
  g.uncertainty_limit,
  g.created_at,
  g.updated_at
FROM form_space.goal_contract g
JOIN form_space.space sp ON sp.id = g.space_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.chart c ON c.id = g.chart_id
LEFT JOIN form_space.target t ON t.id = g.target_id;

DO $$
DECLARE
  rec record;
BEGIN
  FOR rec IN
    SELECT unnest(ARRAY[
      'space','metric','chart','chart_transition','embodiment_binding',
      'target','attractor','goal_contract','trajectory','intervention','recovery_trial'
    ]) AS table_name
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_fs_%I_touch ON form_space.%I',
                   rec.table_name, rec.table_name);
    EXECUTE format(
      'CREATE TRIGGER trg_fs_%I_touch BEFORE UPDATE ON form_space.%I '
      'FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION form_space.touch_updated_at()',
      rec.table_name, rec.table_name
    );
  END LOOP;
END;
$$;
